expl.label: Clause-initial aspectual/raising verbs like 'begin', 'yet (to)', 'upon (us)', 'wish'
expl.positive_pole: Fires on the predicate word right after a subject or auxiliary when it opens a construction that needs a complement, especially an infinitive or verb phrase. Strongest (+7 to +10): begin/began/begins (+ to/V-ing/object: 'you begin to daydream', 'I began looking'); 'yet' in 'has/have/is yet to' (~+8, then 'to' ~+1); 'upon' in '[season/weather] is upon us' and 'upon check-in' (~+8 to +9); 'wish' in 'wish (not) to' (~+8); 'herein' in 'information contained herein' (~+8). Moderate (+2 to +5): modal 'may' (often 'may be required', 'may not', 'may apply'), 'appear(s) to', 'those (of)' as in 'those of the pastor', 'remains' in 'X remains our...', 'bear the name', 'attempted', 'purchased'. Weak (+1 to +2): following 'to', 'be', 'not', 'perhaps', 'however', 'just', 'nor', 'therefore'. The activation sits on the verb or particle itself, not on the complement.
expl.negative_pole: Weak, broad, and diffuse (rarely below -3). It shows up on function words inside formal legal, disclaimer, licensing, and regulatory boilerplate. Examples: 'and', 'are', 'for', 'or', 'about', 'if', 'its', 'of', commas. Typical cases are 'provided the original author and source are(-3) credited', 'Seek medical attention if(-3) irritation persists', 'no warranties or guarantees about(-3)', and 'Evidence-Based(-3)'. Values there run about -1 to -3. The positive triggers like 'may', 'those', and 'herein' still fire positive even inside such text.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for nearly all tokens; only about 0.7% of tokens exceed |1|. Assign the following values. 'begin/began/begins' as a main verb: +7 to +10. 'yet' in 'has/have yet to': +8. 'upon' in 'is upon us' or 'upon arrival/check-in': +8 to +9. 'wish' + to: +8. 'herein': +8. 'may' (modal): +2 to +4. 'appear(s) to', 'remains', 'those of': +3 to +5. Other complement-taking verbs ('attempted', 'reached', 'purchased') and discourse adverbs ('therefore', 'however', 'perhaps'): +1 to +2. The token right after a strong trigger ('to', 'be', 'your'): about +1. Inside disclaimer, legal, or license boilerplate, give scattered function words -1 to -2, occasionally -3. Do NOT fire on 'start/started', ordinary nouns, or 'begin' used as a noun-like label (except capitalized 'Begin' commands, ~+9). Ordinary narrative or descriptive text is 0.

expl.label: Dependence/condition phrases: 'as a function of', 'over a range of', 'at high', 'with'
expl.positive_pole: Prepositions and connectives that introduce the variable or operating condition a quantity depends on or is measured under, usually in technical, scientific or automotive text. Examples: 'as a function OF the load', 'over AN extensive range OF', 'even AT HIGH volume', 'decreases AS it', 'WHEN equipped', 'increases WITH openness', 'regardless OF', 'depending ON', 'depends ON the number', 'independent of level OF', 'stable WITH respect', 'below 100 C', 'above 4500 rpm', 'at LOWER cost', 'gets better WITH age'. The activation sits on the preposition or connective (of/on/with/at/as/over/when/below/above) and spills onto the next 1–3 tokens, which are typically the condition itself (the/an/high/extensive/progressive, or digits of a threshold number).
expl.negative_pole: Weak, at most about -3. It shows up in website boilerplate about accounts, links and access: 'Navigate with this LINK to login', 'we'll SEND YOU a link', 'If you have an account, you CAN', 'please sign in', 'Get Unlimited Archive Access FOR $', 'This is an open-access', 'Full text not available from this repository'. Also faintly (about -1) on 'I've'.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for almost all tokens; the neuron is very sparse.

Positive values:
- +6 to +10: the key preposition in an explicit dependence or operating-range construction. Examples: 'function OF(10) THE(6)', 'over AN(7) extensive(6) range OF(6)', 'at HIGH(6)', 'decreases AS(6)'.
- +3 to +5: secondary cases. Examples: 'when(5) equipped', 'depend ON(4)', 'regardless OF(4)', 'increases WITH(4)', 'stable WITH(4)', 'response to PROGRESSIVE(4)', 'at(4) all' (resistance), 'lower(3) cost', the digits in 'above 4500 rpm' (2–3 each) and 'below 100 C' (space token 5).
- +1 to +2: the tokens just before or after these, such as 'depending', 'friction', 'over THE', 'all mainstream', 'low temperatures'.
- Weaker still: casual uses like 'depends on how much a clan' (1–2).

What does not fire: ordinary prepositions with no sense of a parameter or condition ('the owners of that data', 'on a large scale') stay near 0.

Negative values:
- -1 to -3: login, reset-link, subscribe or access boilerplate. Examples: 'this LINK'(-3), 'account?'(-2), 'will'(-2), 'send you'(-2).

expl.label: Positive: mid-idiom fixed phrases (rest of, true to size); negative: role 'as'
expl.positive_pole: Function words inside conventional multiword idioms and set phrases, firing where the rest of the idiom is highly predictable. Activation sits on the connective or preposition in the middle of the phrase. Examples: 'rest OF' (+6 to +8, as in 'last the rest of', 'for the rest of', 'make it fit the rest of'); 'life OF' in 'for the life of'; 'shape of MY life'; 'true TO size'; 'suit / fits / fit' in 'fit your needs', 'suit their culture'; 'vary slightly FROM what appears ON'; 'stunning IN person than ON'; 'from the beginning TO THE end'; 'as IT gets'; 'wise beyond HIS years'; 'up to AND beyond'; 'made IN', 'measured BY', 'over the course of', 'every time'.
expl.negative_pole: The word 'as' when it introduces a role, function, or capacity: 'use X AS a', 'with the RedHead AS my partner', 'using lottery funding AS a crutch', 'as bait', 'as inspired by', 'as well', 'as a general rule', 'gone AS soon as', 'track my steps AS I strive'. These 'as' tokens hit -7 to -10. The token right after 'as' is also negative: 'a' or 'my' around -4 to -7. Verbs that set up 'as' carry weaker negatives: 'use' and 'them' around -3 to -5. Possessives in a role sense are also mildly negative, e.g. 'Logic was MY crutch' at -7 and 'She's my own' at -4.
expl.rubric: Background is 0; most tokens fall below 0.5. Weak +1 to +3 goes on prepositions, 'it', and verbs inside common collocations. Give +5 to +8 to the highly predictable middle token of a fixed idiom: 'of' after 'rest' or 'life', 'to' in 'true to size', 'fit/fits/suit' before 'your needs/goals', 'to the' in 'from beginning to end', 'in' in 'in person', 'it' in 'as it gets / than it is'. Neighbouring tokens in the same phrase get +2 to +4, e.g. 'rest' +4 and 'the' after 'to' +6. Literal, non-idiomatic prepositions get about 0. Give -7 to -10 to 'as' meaning 'in the role of / serving as' or to set-phrase 'as' ('as well', 'as soon as', 'as a rule'). Give -3 to -5 to the next determiner or possessive and to a preceding 'use ... them'. Comparative 'as' in an 'as X as it gets' frame is not negative; there the following 'it' is positive. Scattered small -1 values appear on adjectives and commas.

expl.label: 'Joint' (shared/combined) token; negative on 'don't know'/'find out'
expl.positive_pole: The word 'joint'/'Joint' meaning shared or combined, especially when it opens an institutional name or a compound: 'Joint Commission', 'Joint Base', 'Joint Typhoon Warning Center', 'JEDEC (Joint Electronic...)', 'joint venture', 'joint declaration', 'Jointly'. The activation sits on the 'joint' token itself. Following tokens get a small spillover ('Electronic' +7, 'ly' +7, 'Typhoon' +2, 'Base' +3). The same concept spreads weakly to other togetherness words: 'jointly', 'joined together', 'join' (song credit), 'Join us/Join Forces', 'co-led', 'Co-authors', and faintly to 'United', 'unified', 'teaming', 'joins'.
expl.negative_pole: Conversational expressions of not knowing or discovery, mostly in dialogue or casual Q&A right after a question: 'I don't know', 'don't care', 'don't want', 'find out', 'Find out the answers', 'Oh'. The negative values fall on 'don't/'t', 'know', 'find', 'out', 'you', and 'I'.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for almost all tokens.

Positive values:
- Capitalized 'Joint' starting an organization name, or 'joint' in a formal compound (venture, declaration, office, commission, base, committee): +8 to +10.
- Generic 'joint' (joint activities, joint project, joint session, joint tenancy, joint gain, joint criminal enterprise): +4 to +7.
- 'jointly': about +4.
- 'joined (together)' meaning combined: about +4.
- The token right after 'Joint' that continues the name: +1 to +7.
- Imperative 'Join' (us / forces / brand): about +3.
- 'co-' prefixes meaning shared (co-led, Co-authors): about +2 to +3.
- 'United', 'unified', 'joins', 'teaming': about +1.
- 'joint' as a body part or cannabis is presumably weaker; give it about +2 to +4.

Negative values:
- 'I don't know…' after a question: 'don't' -3 to -4, 'know' -2 to -3, 'I' -2 to -3.
- 'why don't you find out?': 'find' about -5, 'out' -3, 'you' -3.
- 'Find out' as a teaser: -2 to -3.
- 'Oh' after a question: -1 to -3.
- The preceding '?' or 'Well': about -1.
- Plain 'know', or 'don't' in non-conversational prose, is near 0.

expl.label: Creation verbs: passive 'made/built for/in/from' (neg) vs active make/create (pos)
expl.positive_pole: Weak (mostly +1 to +3). Fires on active, agentive uses of make/create/set/do, landing on the verb or the token just after it. Typical spots are reflexive or object slots like 'set myself', 'make yourself', 'made himself', 'create an account', 'create new', 'establishing a', 'make sure', and 'would do,'. These are cases where the subject is doing the making and the object comes next.
expl.negative_pole: Strong (to -10). Fires on passive or participial creation verbs that describe how or where an artifact was produced. The main trigger is 'made' used as a past participle after a noun: 'card made for', 'sauce made from', 'products made for people', 'movie made on a shoestring', 'rings made in'. Similar participles also fire: built, created, produced, crafted, designed, developed, collected. The negative also lands on the provenance tokens that follow: 'specially', 'In' (as in 'Made In India'), 'out of', 'for', 'with', 'from'. A further trigger is a made object in 'make a small boat out of' and 'made it just for you', where the negative falls on 'boat', 'out', 'it', and 'just'.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0; almost all tokens score 0.

Negative values:
- Participle 'made' right after a noun (artifact made for/from/in/on/with): -8 to -10.
- Other production participles (built with, created by, produced in, handcrafted, developed in, designed): -3 to -9.
- The following preposition or adverb (for, in, from, with, out, of, specially, just): -1 to -9. It can exceed the verb, e.g. 'made specially' gives 'specially' -9.
- A noun that is the made object followed by 'out of'/'from': -5 to -8.
- Weaker cases: 'by Admin' after 'Written' -2 to -3; 'plan strategies around' -4.

Positive values:
- Active imperative or first-person make/create/set/do with an object or reflexive next, e.g. 'make yourself', 'set myself', 'create an account', 'make sure', 'got started on': +1 to +3 on the verb or the next token.
- Positives rarely exceed +3.

Does not fire:
- Generic nouns.
- 'made' in perfect tense with no provenance phrase gives a near-zero or small positive value.

expl.label: Onset of an alternate rendering: translation, gloss, variant spelling, or equivalent
expl.positive_pole: Fires where the text is about to give, or has just begun giving, an alternative form of a term it just named. This covers translations (Hoshi no Kirby (星のカービィ; Lola la Chata ("Snub-Nose"); Tres Grandes; Nuestra Salud), pronunciations (pronounced "pickpocket"; [laːɣə]), variant spellings or minimal pairs (loathe vs. loath; Program & Programme; Gamoe (or Garmo)), parallel glosses (Basque = oliba, Finnish = olivi; yard (garden); carpe diem – seize the day) and acronym or parenthetical renamings (Pension fund (KWAP)). The peak usually sits on the separator that introduces the alternative: 'vs.', '(', '=', '&', 'or', 'pronounced', or an opening quote. It can also sit on the first one to three tokens of the alternative itself, especially foreign-script characters (Japanese, Devanagari, Korean, Chinese) or a translated phrase (the cursed souls).
expl.negative_pole: Weak only, at most about -2. It appears on the opening words of repeated titles or set phrases, such as 'Watch Love Is All You Need', 'WHAT DOESN'T', 'e-mail is unsubscribed', 'Intellectual rigour', 'No Regulation Without Representation', or table pipe separators. It is mostly negligible.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for nearly all tokens. Assign these values: 8-10 on the separator or first token of an explicit contrastive or variant pair (e.g., the '.' in 'loathe vs.' and ' lo' of 'loath'), or on an opening '(' or '“' immediately before a translation or nickname. Give 5-8 to the first characters or words of a foreign-script or translated equivalent (の, カ, ल, Tres, Grandes, Nuestra, the second '&' in 'Program & Programme &'). Give 3-5 to glosses like '= ' in a language list, 'pronounced', '(' before a substitute word, or the ' G' in '(or Garmo)'. Give 1-3 to an ordinary '(' before an acronym expansion ('(KWAP)', '(EDCA)', '(AGC)'), to quoted nicknames (Edward "Ted"), to 'means "', and to the later tokens of the rendered alternative. A generic parenthesis or quote with no equivalence relation gets about 0. Negative values of -1 to -2 go only to the starts of repeated titles or slogans; never assign below -2.

expl.label: Preposition 'for' in stock idioms (for free/for that/for any purpose); sparse negative spikes
expl.positive_pole: Strongest on the preposition 'for' when it begins a short, highly predictable idiomatic or boilerplate completion: 'Claim your listing for| free' (+9), 'there's an essential oil for| that' (+8), 'for| any purpose' in legal disclaimers (+6), 'a bad movie for| sure' (+3). The token right after can carry a small residue ('to' +3, 'any' +2). Weaker secondary triggers, around +3 to +4: 'Welcome' opening a website greeting ('Welcome to ...'); 'all' in 'agree with everything all the authors'; 'entries' in 'zero entries'; 'kind' in 'each kind of'; 'You' starting an instruction sentence; the final digits/'paper' in citation strings; 'reproduction' in Creative Commons licence text.
expl.negative_pole: Rare, isolated, hard-to-predict spikes inside templated, SEO or spammy commercial text, code and math. Examples: the comma after '4k' in '4k, HD Wallpaper' (-10); ')' in '(G)' (-9); 'for' in 'tap and hold for seven second' (-9); 'growth' in 'size and growth, segmentation' in market-report spam (-9); 'you' in 'expert can help you' (-8); 'shipping' in 'free shipping' (-5); a closing quote; ')' or '))' closing code or math expressions (-5); 'even' in 'even more' (-5); 'for' in 'best company to work for' (-4). These are usually single tokens, often closing punctuation or a key noun or pronoun in a boilerplate list.
expl.rubric: Background: most tokens are 0. About 6% of tokens carry ±1 noise, scattered fairly evenly in both directions, with slight positive drift in lists and recipes. Scoring rules: 1) 'for' introducing a fixed idiom completion such as 'for free', 'for that', 'for any purpose' or 'for sure' gets +6 to +9, and the next token gets +1 to +3. 2) 'Welcome' at the start of a site greeting gets about +3, and the following 'to' gets +1 to +2. 3) Other idiom or list heads ('each kind', 'zero entries', 'all the', end of a citation number) get +2 to +4. 4) 'for' meaning a duration ('for seven second') or stranded at the end of a clause ('to work for') can go strongly negative, about -4 to -9. 5) Rare negative spikes of -5 to -10 land on punctuation or a key token inside templated product, wallpaper or market-report spam, or on closing brackets in code or math. Anything with |value| ≥ 3 is very rare, about 6 in 100k tokens, so default to 0 or ±1 unless one of the patterns above is clear.

expl.label: Copula and predicate in 'X is/are a/required/trademarks' classification statements (negative)
expl.positive_pole: Weak and diffuse. Small values (+1 to +3) fall on second-person or relational copulas and their articles in affectionate or devotional address ("You are the Most Merciful", "You are forever part of me", "they are the one"). Similar small values appear on report table-of-contents tokens ("Revenue (Value) by Region (2013"), on the colon before anagram word lists, and on a few FAQ or vendor phrases ("Are you factory?", "a trusted vendor"). Rarely exceeds +3.
expl.negative_pole:
The main pole. It fires on the copula and the start of the predicate in a statement that assigns its subject a category, status or requirement, especially in boilerplate.
- The strongest token is usually the copula "are"/"is" or the article right after it: "Fields marked with an asterisk (*) are required" (are = -10), "HID and the HID logo are trademarks or registered trademarks of" (are, trademarks, or = -5 to -7), "It is a beloved irrational" (a = -6), "The Division is currently a safe Liberal seat" (a = -6), "Conjugate is a scrabble word" (is -4, a -5).
- It also fires on the possessive or brand in "one of our specialty" (our = -5), "one of China's Spring Cities" ('s = -5), "is an Amazon Bestseller" (Amazon = -6) and "one of my new pieces" (my = -3).
- It also hits "* Required Fields" (Required = -5), "are \"forward-looking statements\"" and "is not my first language".
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 on nearly all tokens; only about 0.07% of tokens reach |1|.

Negative values:
- -6 to -10: the copula or article in legal or form boilerplate classifications, such as "(*) are required", "are trademarks or registered trademarks", "is a [category noun]" in encyclopedia-like definitions, or "is currently a safe seat".
- -3 to -5: the following predicate noun or adjective ("required", "trademarks", "specialty"); possessives or brands after "one of" / "is an"; and "Required" in "* Required Fields".
- -1 to -2: the subject-phrase tokens just before the copula ("marked", "Group", "*") and tokens after the predicate head.
- A plain copula in narrative with no categorical predicate gets about 0 to -1.

Positive values:
- +1 to +3: "You are" / "are the" in devotional or affectionate address.
- +1 to +3: TOC or report-style parentheticals such as "(Value) by Region (2013".
- +1 to +2: a colon starting a word list.
- Otherwise assign 0.

expl.label: Customer-transaction outcomes: value, delay, or service received
expl.positive_pole: Clauses in consumer, service or commercial prose that describe what a customer gets out of a transaction or service: how much value per payment ('less fuel for your money', 'more burn for your buck', 'the full price', 'full refund'), how long service takes or when it happens ('took forever to get the food', 'take too long to get a load', 'allow a few extra days for us to order this before sending it out', 'get back to you with more information', 'get the work back to me'), and whether things work or perform as expected ('refrigerators no longer seem to work efficiently', 'it just doesn't fit', 'ready and willing to help'). Activation builds across the phrase and peaks on mid-phrase function or relation words: 'for', 'before', 'to', 'with', 'back', 'the', 'longer', 'by' (as in '100 pellets by box'). The noun after the peak is usually lower.
expl.negative_pole: Weaker, max about -5. Fires on instructional, motivational, sports or product-feature prose about directing, positioning or supporting something. Examples: 'Go confidently in the direction of your dreams' (-5 on 'of'/'your'), 'guard your man' (-5), 'I feel they are the most talented' (-4), 'optimal spine support', 'helps golfers with an…', 'collars should fit comfortably on the dog's neck', 'as you can afford it', 'keep hold of the'. Peaks fall on prepositions, possessives or verbs inside these advisory or descriptive phrases.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 on most tokens. Only about 2% of tokens reach |1|, and above |5| is very rare. Rules for positive values: (1) Commercial or consumer context, such as reviews, shop policies, service ads, refunds, shipping or pricing: give +1 to +2 to many tokens across the sentence. (2) The phrase states a value-for-money, delay/turnaround, or performance/outcome relation: give +4 to +7 on the key connector or verb ('to', 'get', 'back', 'with', 'longer'). (3) Peak relation word in a strong case ('for' in 'fuel for your money', 'before' in 'before sending it out'): +8 to +10. Tokens just after the peak get +2 to +5. Rules for negative values: in advice, sports or product-spec descriptions of direction, position, fit or support, give -1 to -2 to scattered tokens and -3 to -5 on the peak preposition, possessive or verb. Exclusions: ordinary narrative, news and technical text give about 0. Price or number words alone without the outcome framing give only about +1. Generic 'your' in instructions tends to be slightly negative rather than positive.

expl.label: Digit-continuation neuron: negative on the token right after a leading '7', positive on mid-number '2'
expl.positive_pole: Mid-number digit tokens, mostly '2' (sometimes '4' or '3'), that come after a multi-digit prefix not ending in 7. Examples: ZIP 97«2»02, 53«2»12, 7«2»035, 47«4»48; Form 53«2»9; price 0.67«2»0. Peaks are moderate, about +2 to +4. Very weak (+1 to +2) on a name fragment right after a short capitalised syllable like Sad/Nad (Sad«hb»ela, Sad«iv», Nad«ine»), and on odd tokens like ' Pediatric'. Also about +1 on a hyphen inside a phone number (800-853«-»1403).
expl.negative_pole: The token immediately after a digit token '7', strongest when that next token is '0'. Examples: phone area codes 7«0»3 and (7«0»8) at -10, 7«0»1-10 at -8, ZIP 7«0»345 at -7, NCC-17«0»1 at -6, 77«0»43 at -5, 7.«0» at -4, 07«0» at -2. Other followers of '7' are weaker. '1' after 7 (7«1»3, 7«1»8) gives about -3. ':' after 7 in Bible references (Luke 7«:»3, Matthew 7«:»11) gives about -4, and the digit after that colon about -3. A hyphen after 7-then-0 (EF 70«-»300) gives about -4. 'c' after 7 inside a hex string gives about -2 to -4. The effect is mostly confined to that one token after the 7.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for almost all tokens, including ordinary prose and most numbers.
1. Find each digit token '7'. Score the very next token:
   - '0': -5 to -10 (strongest in phone area codes and ZIP or model-number starts).
   - '1' or ':': -3 to -4.
   - '3', '-', or a hex letter: -1 to -4.
   - Tokens two or more places after the 7: usually small, about -1.
2. A '2' (or occasionally '4') in the middle of a ZIP, form number or decimal, after a prefix like 97, 53, 47, 67 or 7: +2 to +4.
3. Other mid-number digits: 0 to +1. A hyphen inside a phone number: -2 to +1.
4. A name-continuation fragment after a short capitalised syllable (Sad-, Nad-, Dard-): about +1 to +2.
5. The '7' itself, and digits not following a 7, stay near 0. Isolated '0' not after 7 stays 0, as do prose words.

expl.label: Nouns naming a component, section, or region within a structured whole
expl.positive_pole: Fires on the content noun that names a sub-part or element inside a larger structure, especially in descriptions of layout, composition, or contents. Examples: "polygon" (map region), "section"/"sections", "icons" on a desktop, "panes: one", "box next to", "charges" on a bill, "entries" in a matrix, "boundaries" of octets, "line going up", "frequency range", "spaces", "flecks", "pieces", "forums", "categories", "rule(s)". Typical frames are "there will be a ___", "contains ___", "features boxed ___", "cut into 4 equal ___" and "two panes: one". The activation sits on the part-noun itself, or on the "one" that picks out a part. Neighboring words (prepositions, determiners, a following "that"/"going up") get small values of +1 to +3.
expl.negative_pole:
Weaker (down to about -5) and more diffuse. Main triggers:
- Spending and resource words: "spent", "expend precious", "funds", "Monies raised".
- Named formal entities: "Memorial Award", "Endowment Advisory Council", "correction functions".
- UI instruction targets: "click the >> icon", "Ctrl+P", "USE keyword", "click again", "the star".
- Clause-ending list words: "respectively,".
- Possessive and life-devotion phrasing: "devoted her", "reserved for".
- Years and numbers in legal or financial text.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for nearly all tokens; only about 0.6% of tokens reach |1|.

Positive scale:
- +8 to +10: a concrete part or region noun in a spatial or structural description, e.g. "polygon representing the region", "a section to upload".
- +4 to +6: icons, sections, panes/one, charges, entries, boundaries, line, range, forums, box, spaces, time (as a component of a total).
- +2 to +4: a weaker part noun such as line, pieces, ribbons, ways, column, or a parenthetical unit like "(".
- +1 to +2: nearby function words in the same phrase, and generic list items such as text, taps, categories, house.

Negative scale:
- -3 to -5: money or effort expenditure (spent, expend, funds, monies), proper-noun institutional names (Award, Endowment, Council), keyboard shortcuts and clicked UI elements, "respectively,".
- -1 to -2: instruction verbs (click, follow, use, go), "steps", "required", digits in dates or amounts.

What does not fire positively: abstract nouns, verbs, and part nouns used as clicking targets in instructions ("click the icon" goes negative, while "desktop hosts icons" goes positive).

expl.label: The word 'shape' and its inflections (shaped, shapes, shaping)
expl.positive_pole: Tokens of the lexeme 'shape' in any sense: shape, shapes, shaped, shaping, Shape. This covers physical form ('shape of your eyebrows', 'Mat Shape: Round'), the verb meaning to influence ('shape the future'), 'shaping up to be', 'in the best shape', and '-shaped' compounds. It also fires on the subword 'Sh'+'ap' pieces, as in 'Shapely' or the place name 'Shap'. Activation sits on the shape token itself. The following token ('of', 'up', 'like', 'and', '&', 'your') often gets a small +1 to +4 echo.
expl.negative_pole: Weak and negligible. Values of about -1 to -3 appear on mid-word subword fragments of unusual proper names (Ber|en|ice, Ber|z|ukov, Nerl|ens) and on digits/hyphens in phone numbers like 888-4. Rarely exceeds -1.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for nearly all tokens. 'shape/shaped/shapes/shaping/Shape' as a standalone word token: +6 to +10. The highest values come from product and descriptive contexts like 'pneumatic shaped', 'shaping up to', 'all shapes and sizes', and 'Shape Body Case'. 'Sh'+'ap' subword pieces (Shapely, Shap): +8 to +9. Abstract or idiomatic uses ('best shape of my life', 'help shape the attitude', 'irregularly shaped', 'took shape'): +2 to +5. Hyphenated '-shaped' attached to a prior word: about +2. The next token after 'shape' ('of', 'up', 'like', 'and'): +1 to +4, with 'of' strongest. Related form words such as silhouette, form, curves, molded, mould, design, and contour: only +1 to +2, often 0; do not overpredict these. Unrelated words containing similar letters get 0. Negative values: -1 on odd name fragments or phone-number digits, with -3 the maximum.

expl.label: Negative: 'Ni/NI' name-starts and 'came up'; weak positive: mid-syllables of foreign names
expl.positive_pole: Weak (+1 to +2) activations on internal subword pieces of foreign or unusual proper names, typically a middle syllable that is often i-containing: A«ki»hito, Wojc«ick»i, Vu«ji»ć, Acc«i»ardo, Ad«ich»ie, Kaoh«si»ung, Tosh«iki». There is very occasional faint activation on generic phrases ('account for free').
expl.negative_pole: Strong negative activation on a word-initial 'Ni'/'NI'/'ni' token that begins a name or acronym: Niemczewski, Niels, NIKE, NIWA, Niang, Niagara, niqab, El Niño. Weaker cases are 'Nic'/'Nick' and Quinn«ip»iac. A second trigger is 'up' in 'came/come up' (come up short, came up empty, came up with).
expl.rubric: Background is 0 almost everywhere. Negative values: ' Ni'/'NI' starting a proper noun or acronym (Niels, NIKE, Niemczewski) = -7 to -10. 'up' after came/come = -7 to -9 in 'came up short/empty', about -4 to -7 in 'came up with'. Mid-name 'Ni'/'i' after a hyphen (Buffalo-Niagara) = -7. ' Nic'/' Nick' = -3 to -5. 'El Niño' = -3. 'Quinnipiac' 'ip' = -3. 'Monic' in Monicuzza = -1 to -2. The token right after 'Ni' (em, ang, KE, q) = -1 to -4. Positive values: an internal syllable of a non-English surname or place name ('ki', 'ick', 'ji', 'ich', 'si', 'li') = +1 to +2. Ordinary words, plain English names, and 'up' outside the came/come construction ≈ 0.

expl.label: Visual attention/gaze directed at a target (+) vs. physical placement of body/accessories (−)
expl.positive_pole: Seeing, watching, noticing, or drawing attention toward a person or thing. It fires on the token right after a perception or attention verb, which is usually the object pronoun or determiner of the thing being looked at. It also fires on the perception verb itself and on preposition links like 'at', 'to', 'from'. Examples: 'see|6', 'watching his|7 operation', 'watching us and taking|6 stock', 'pointed his baton at|6 me', 'draws the eye to|6', 'draws attention to your|5', 'notice a|5 big group', 'aware of the many pairs of eyes that were watching|5 her|4', 'expose their|6 uniform', 'pull away from your|6 midsection', 'make your|5 face look red', 'noticeable|5 ribs', 'accentuates|6'. Overall theme: visibility, being seen, gaze or attention aimed at a target.
expl.negative_pole: Physically placing, covering, resting, or moving a body part or worn accessory. It peaks on the preposition or possessive after a placement or covering verb, and on accessory nouns. Examples: 'hid my teary face under|-10 my|-8 hair', 'lowered|-6 her|-4 head|-4', 'placed|-6 her hands on|-4 his', 'flopped|-6 back on|-3 the couch', 'perfect for|-5 resting|-6 your|-6 feet', 'doffs|-5 his|-5 hat', 'glasses flung|-5', 'wrap|-5 back up'. Words for sunglasses and eyewear such as 'Sunglasses|-7', 'aviator sunglasses|-5' and 'sunglass|-4' are strongly negative. Clothing and accessory nouns like sweater, gloves and wristwatch give weak negatives of −1 to −3.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for nearly all tokens; generic text and non-physical narration stay at 0.

Positive scale:
- +5 to +7: the pronoun, determiner or preposition right after a visual-perception or attention verb (see/watch/notice/point at/draw attention to/catch sight of), or the strongest such verb itself.
- +2 to +4: neighbouring tokens in the phrase, such as 'of', 'to', the verb when the peak falls on the next token, and 'opposite'.
- +1: weak spillover such as 'to', 'can', 'and' before the verb.

Negative scale:
- −6 to −10: covering, hiding, lowering or placing body parts, and resting feet or the body, on the preposition, possessive or verb.
- −4 to −7: eyewear nouns.
- −1 to −3: other clothing and accessory nouns, and verbs for handling objects (hold, clip, pull a chair).

Non-visual mental verbs (think, know) and abstract 'see' meaning 'understand' in boilerplate ('click here to see a list') reach only about +1. Ordinary physical actions without body-part or accessory placement stay near 0.

expl.label: Negative: slot before a subset quantifier (some/others/most/%). Positive: beneficiary 'for/to'
expl.positive_pole: Weaker pole, max about +5. It fires on prepositions and function words that introduce a recipient, beneficiary or target of an action. The strongest case is boilerplate: 'We have a modified experience **for** viewers using ad blockers' (Wikia): 'for' +5, neighbouring 'experience' and 'viewers' +1–2. Similar cases: 'set a positive example **for** my children' (+3), 'shared **with** anyone' (+3), 'attracted **to** a charged rod' (+3), 'fill **in** the details' (+3), 'read this **and** access all' (+4), 'only best-selling authors' (+3), 'you can **edit**' (+3). These are mostly in instructional or site-policy text addressed to a reader or user.
expl.rubric:
Background: 0 on almost all tokens. Fewer than 0.5% of tokens reach |value| ≥ 1.

Negative values:
- -8 to -10: the token just before 'others', 'most', 'many', 'one', 'the other(s)' or a percentage, when a contrast/partition of a population has already been set up. Typical setups are 'While some…', 'some… ,', '…in 15 countries while…', 'In some…'.
- -3 to -5: the same position with a weaker or absent contrast frame. Examples: 'starting in two of them', 'Unfortunately, for many of', 'rated … by our readers', 'connected to 0 board members', 'but' after a concession.
- -1 to -2: the quantifier itself ('some', 'most'), earlier tokens in the frame, and words such as 'subscriber', 'register', 'surprising'.

Positive values:
- +5: 'for' in 'modified experience for viewers'.
- +2 to +4: a beneficiary/recipient preposition or conjunction pointing at a specific person or object ('for my three children', 'with anyone', 'to a charged rod', 'and access'). This also covers user-facing action verbs in site text ('edit', 'delete').
- +1: surrounding verbs and nouns in instructions or policy text.

Prepositions not followed by a beneficiary or a group-partition quantifier stay near 0.

expl.label: Intensity/gravity adjectives: 'serious(ly)', 'grave', 'severe' (harm-related)
expl.positive_pole: Fires on the token for the word 'serious'/'seriously' and close synonyms of gravity, such as 'grave' and 'severe'. It fires most when they describe harm: injury, illness, side effects, risk, consequences or mistakes. Other figurative uses of 'serious' also fire strongly ('serious business', 'in serious time', 'I seriously couldn't'). The concept extends weakly to related severity or magnitude words: 'critical', 'Severity', 'fatal', 'catastrophic', 'major', 'significant', 'gross(ly)', 'death(ly)'. 'Graveside' and 'Gravestone' also fire (+8) on the 'Gr-av' subword, by surface overlap with 'grave'.
expl.negative_pole: Negligible. There are faint values near -1 to -2 on copulas and possessives in religious statements ('God is love', 'He is my God', 'God is a holy...'), plus a few random tokens. These are essentially background.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for nearly all tokens. Put the value on the severity word itself.
- 'serious' or 'seriously' (any sense, strongest with harm/medical/legal contexts): +7 to +10.
- 'grave' (adjective) and 'Grav-' in grave(side/stone): +8 to +10.
- 'severe': +4 to +5.
- 'Severity', 'fatal', 'critical': +3 to +4.
- 'major', 'catastrophic', 'significant', 'grossly', 'deathly', 'horrible': +1 to +2.
- Following tokens get small spillover. Examples: 'illness'/'health'/'or' +1; 'life-threatening' 'threatening' +4, '-life' +2; 'medical' +3; a comma after 'serious' +3; 'nature of the' +1 to +2.
- Generic negative or emotional words without the gravity/severity sense (e.g., 'dangerous', 'bad', 'killed') get ~0.
- Religious 'is/my/a' tokens: -1 to -2 at most.

expl.label: + peril/escape motion narratives; − calm creatures/people placidly present nearby
expl.positive_pole: Narrative clauses about dramatic physical motion, danger, entrapment or escape involving an agent. Activation sits on the directional preposition, particle or determiner that follows the action verb, i.e. on the path or source being set up: 'left the infant IN a', 'throw another boy OFF a ramp TO', 'pulled OUT of', 'fell DOWN THE stairs', 'leave him BEHIND for', 'break out OF prison', 'save her FROM a', 'run away FROM the', 'into THE pen', 'cat out OF the bag', 'water to flow OUT'. A weaker version fires on suspenseful questions in a narrative, such as 'know WHY they've been', '"Why...', 'and WHAT secret', 'ask WHAT is happening'.
expl.negative_pole: Calm, descriptive text about animals or people being placidly present or behaving in an ordinary way, often with proximity or location. Strongest on the noun and the following predicate or quantity words: 'animals were out', 'some ONLY a FEW FEET AWAY', 'farm ANIMALS', 'shy CREATURES CAN fill', 'bulls in the nearby PASTURE STAYED AWAY', 'LOCALS REMAIN close', 'socialized WELL WITH children', 'People in cars tend TO notice... if THEY', 'smiling faces AT every', 'stop by and say hello', 'citizens with mental health issues are more likely TO be INVOLVED IN incidents', 'failing to STOP AT a stop sign'. This covers friendly, everyday, traffic or wildlife-viewing contexts, which the neuron treats as the opposite of peril.
expl.rubric:
The background level is 0, and most tokens are 0.

Positive values:
- +3 to +4: the preposition, particle or determiner right after a peril or motion verb in a story (in/off/out/of/from/to/down/the/behind/into).
- +1 to +2: the verb itself and nearby tokens.
- +2 to +3: a suspense question word (why/what) in a narrative.
- +1: mild quest or escape language.

Negative values:
- −5 to −10: 'only a few feet away' near animals, 'farm animals', 'creatures can', 'locals remain', 'they' in 'even if they' about people noticing, 'stayed away' of livestock, 'stop by' / 'make sure to'.
- −2 to −4: surrounding words in calm descriptions of animals or people and their whereabouts or behavior (wildlife, buffalo, people are pleasant, smiling faces at).
- −1 to −3: mild cases such as dates, or reviews saying 'people were nice'.

Do not fire on generic prepositions in non-narrative prose, such as menus, business text or sports recaps (0). Similar spatial words like 'away' and 'close' go negative when describing calm proximity and positive only when describing fleeing or danger.

expl.label: Word-initial 'Mon'/'MON' token (Mon-, Monster, Monkey, Monitor); negative on farm/earth/cake
expl.positive_pole: Fires on the first token of a capitalized word beginning with 'Mon'. This covers 'Mon' as a piece (Monet, Monique, Monarch, Monahan, Monsoon, Monopoint, Monice, Monic-uzza, Monastrell, Monk), whole-word tokens like Monster, Monkey and Monitor, and all-caps MON (MON810, MONSTERS, MONSTROSITY). Lowercase 'monitor' and 'monopol' also fire, but more weakly. The peak sits on the 'Mon' token. The following subword token often gets a smaller positive value (+1 to +4), for example 'et', 'ST', 'k', 'arch'. 'Monday' fires only moderately (~+4). Secondary weak activations: semicolons in odd or garbled contexts (+4 to +9), 'which' after a noun or comma (+2 to +4), 'mode' in 'single-mode', and scattered abstract nouns (+1 to +2).
expl.negative_pole: Moderate negative values, about -3 to -5, on agrarian or earthy nouns: farm, farmers, Farmer('s), Farm, earth/earthy, cake, floor, snow. Also occasionally on '…' and some proper names (Saudi, Matthew), about -3. The token after one of these nouns, such as 'that' or 'y', is often mildly negative (-1 to -3).
expl.rubric: Background is ~0 on most tokens; scattered ±1 values are common. Capitalized word-initial Mon/MON token, or a whole-word token starting with Mon (Monster, Monkey, Monitor): +8 to +10. Lowercase monitor: ~+9. Monopol-: ~+3. Monday: ~+4. Continuation subword right after Mon: +1 to +4. Semicolon in junk or encoded strings: +4 to +9. Normal-prose semicolon: ~+4. 'which' in relative clauses: +2 to +4. Words merely containing 'mon' mid-word (e.g. 'common', 'lemon'): ~0. 'Money', 'month', 'Mont-': likely weak, uncertain. farm/farmers/Farmer/earth/cake/floor: -4 to -5. Snow, Saudi, '…', Matthew: ~-3. Other food or nature nouns (pumpkin, wine, fireworks, fashion): -1 to -2.

expl.label: Slot anticipating a required state or duty (keep X ___, fail to ___)
expl.positive_pole: Fires on the token right before a predicted state or obligation is named, in constructions about keeping, ensuring or failing to meet a condition. The activation sits on the slot, not on the state word itself. Typical slots: the object or subject just before the state word, as in "keep your head|10 upright", "help keep feet|9 dry", "make sure the ground is|10 level", "keep all interested parties|7 informed" and "keeping your feet|7". The "to" in failure-to-comply phrases, as in "failure to|10 file", "FAILURE TO|9 FILE", "fails to|8 make", "failing to|7 pay" and "failed to|7 maintain". Connectives inside a list of desired qualities, such as "clear,|8 concise,|4 and|5", "Store in a|7 cool,|5 dry", "clean,|7 vegetarian", "sitting up straight and|7 maintaining" and "wet but|8 not". Also negated performance verbs, as in "didn't|7 perform" and "weren't|7", and "ensure|7" or "to get|7 sharp" when a goal state is coming.
expl.negative_pole: Weaker (down to about -4). Fires on the maintaining or preserving verb itself and on the state phrase it governs. Examples: "maintain|-4" ("maintaining|-4 and improving", "cells maintain|-4 their|-2 shape"), "Keep|-4 warm|-2", "tries to keep|-4 things", "holds|-4 its definition", "restored to|-4 'like new'", "helps keep Airbnb a|-4 safe|-3 and|-3 trusted", "must still|-3 be|-4 managed", "trying|-4". Also scattered -1 to -4 values on odd subword pieces of names or numbers ("C IV|-4", "F|-3ifty", "Sh-ol|-3").
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 on almost all tokens, with only occasional ±1 noise. Only about 1.5% of tokens reach |1|.

Positive values:
- +7 to +10: the slot token directly before an expected condition after keep/help keep/make sure/ensure (object noun or copula), and "to" after failure/fail/failing.
- +3 to +8: commas, "and" or "but" linking desired-state adjectives (cool, dry; clear, concise).
- +1 to +3: surrounding words in these constructions (the state word itself, "failure", "file", "timely").

The state word that follows the slot usually gets only +1 to +3. The most predictive cue is a token where the model expects the next word to name the state to be kept or the duty to be done.

Negative values:
- -2 to -4: the verbs maintain/keep/hold/restore and their immediate state complements when the verb itself is the token.
- About -1: legal or list nouns such as "conspiracy", "bank fraud" and "of".

Ordinary prose without keep/ensure/fail-to framing stays at 0.

expl.label: Verb/preposition heads (−) and following anaphoric determiners like this/that/same (+)
expl.positive_pole: Weak, at most about +3. Fires on the determiner or adjective that opens an object noun phrase pointing back to something already mentioned or evaluating it: "this/that/these/este" + noun ("this task", "this project", "that problem", "this road", "that label"), "the same" ("the same situation"), "such a" + adjective ("such a simple task", "such a crucial issue"), and evaluative words in that slot ("all-important", "simple", "feminine", "great"). It usually follows a verb or preposition (on/to/for/in/accomplish/wear). Copulas and deictic subjects get small values too ("is", "That's", "This is a", "these are all").
expl.negative_pole:
Fires on the verb or preposition head that governs a following object, especially when that object is a repeated, previously mentioned or specific thing. The strongest cases are speech or report verbs about repeating content:
- "Had you asked(−10) me(−8) the(−4) same question"
- "I have asked(−6) this question"
- "I've probably said(−5) this"
- "many users have reported(−5) that", "came across(−5)"
Other examples:
- "held(−5) the top slot", "make(−5) this up"
- "modify(−4) your payment info", "Not including(−4) the required"
- "since I last taught(−4)", "made(−3) the comments", "goes about(−3) it"
- Bid boilerplate: "for/para(−4/−5) this job/este trabajo"
The pronoun or article right after the verb can also be negative ("me", "the"). Weak −1 to −3 values appear on light verbs and prepositions ("on", "to", "see", "do", "when", "last time", "the only place … where").
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for almost every token; only about 0.2% of tokens reach |value| ≥ 1.
- −8 to −10: transitive verb (and its pronoun object) introducing a repeated or anaphoric object, as in "asked me the same question". Very rare.
- −4 to −6: verb or preposition heads before a definite or demonstrative object ("asked", "said", "reported", "held", "make … up", "modify", "including", "for this job").
- −1 to −3: lighter verbs, prepositions, "to", "when", "time", "place".
- +1 to +3: the demonstrative or anaphoric determiner or adjective directly after such a head ("this", "that", "these", "este", "same", "such a", "simple", "all-important"). The following noun is about +1.
The sign typically flips across a phrase: negative on the head, positive on the determiner. Positive values never exceed about +3 in practice. Ordinary content words, nouns and descriptive text with no object-taking head stay at 0. A bare "this" at the start of a sentence gives only about +1.

expl.label: Negative: 'when it comes to' topic-restricting phrase; weak positive 'as far as'
expl.positive_pole: Very weak (about +1). It appears on the 'far' of 'as far as', on 'right'/'wrong' in 'X is right / I was wrong', on 'view' in 'point of view', on 'questions' in 'with any questions you may have', and on 'date'/'updated' in 'kept up to date'. These are mostly scope or perspective framing expressions. Positive values essentially never go above about +1.
expl.negative_pole: Strong. It fires on the phrase 'when it comes to' that follows an evaluative claim about someone or something ('X is the best / an ace / hopeless / experienced ... when it comes to Y'). 'when' and 'it' carry most of the activation, roughly -5 to -10 each. 'comes' gets about -1 to -2, and 'to' gets almost nothing. The same pattern applies to variants such as 'when it pertains to', 'when it is a question of', and 'when considering' after a comparison. Preceding evaluative words ('hopeless', 'trust', 'offer', 'king', 'character', 'experienced') can reach about -1 to -2. The 'as' of 'as far as' gets about -1 to -2.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 on nearly all tokens. For a 'when it comes to' phrase preceded by a judgment or comparison, give 'when' -5 to -10 and 'it' -3 to -8. Score 'comes' at -1 to -2, 'to' at 0, and the evaluative word just before at -1 to -2. Use weaker values (-1 to -3) for 'when it comes to' without a strong evaluative setup, for a sentence-initial 'When' in a related scope sense, and for 'when considering'. For 'as far as', score 'as' -1 to -2, 'far' +1, and the following 'I' -1. Give about +1 to 'right'/'wrong' when judging a person's claim, 'view' in 'point of view', 'questions'/'have' in boilerplate like 'any questions you may have', and 'date' in 'up to date'. Ordinary temporal 'when' ('when you go', 'when she was 19') scores 0, as do 'it' elsewhere and 'comes' elsewhere.

expl.label: Attribute nouns (+) vs. information/content nouns as disclaimer subjects (−)
expl.positive_pole: Moderate activations (+2 to +5) on nouns that name a property, quantity or attribute belonging to some entity. Examples: name / names(ake) / nameless ("the song's name is", "as the name states", "victim's name has not been released"); value / valuations; price tag; numbers; current; space; data in a quota sense ("1 GB data plan", "data allowance"); answer ("the female answer to"); material support; picture of life; details. Often the following copula or verb also gets a smaller positive value (is/has/been +2 to +4), as in "space is a premium" and "name has not been released". Weak positives (+1) appear on numbers, units and scattered concrete nouns. A small positive also shows on "we have clearly explained" inside privacy text.
expl.negative_pole: Strong negatives on generic information/content mass nouns that serve as the subject or topic of a meta-statement about that material, typically in website disclaimers, privacy policies, data-handling text or reviews. Examples: "The information provided...", "All the data are provided as...", "Content posted on...", "The opinions expressed in this Newsletter", "information transmitted from your computer", "the content is what you want", "the data in the bean is", "fact checking", "Everything is super". The noun itself carries the peak (−6 to −10). The following verbs and words (is, provided, posted, collected, will be, are) get −1 to −4. Similar nouns inside the same kind of text but not as the clause subject are weaker (−1 to −4): "more information at", "files on your web site", "values", "things you need", "evidence", "suggestions".
expl.rubric:
Background: 0 for nearly all tokens; only about 1% of tokens reach |value|≥1.

Negative scale:
- −8 to −10: an information/data/content/opinions noun, or the totalizer "Everything", heading a disclaimer-like clause. Examples: "The information", "All the data are", "Content posted", "information transmitted".
- −3 to −5: "your data will be", "data" in programming or storage contexts, "more information", "files", "values", "things you need".
- −1 to −4: the verbs and auxiliaries right after such a noun (is, provided, will be, collected, posted).

Positive scale:
- +3 to +5: attribute nouns of an entity. Examples: name, namesake, value, price, numbers, current, space, data plan/allowance, answer, tipsheet, valuations, "results may vary".
- +1 to +4: a copula following an attribute noun.
- +1: numbers and units in statistics.

Decision rule: words like "information" and "data" go negative when the text treats them as content being described or disclaimed. They go positive only when they act as a measured quantity or attribute ("3GB data allowance", "Electronic Data Interchange" +3).

expl.label: Clause junctions in formal/procedural prose (+); 'for' in Wikia ad-blocker boilerplate (−)
expl.positive_pole:
Function-word and punctuation tokens at clause or sentence junctions in formal, legal, scientific or procedural prose, where the text is about to launch into its next step or item. Strongest cases:
- ', and' that joins a second clause or list item: 'notice and any other', 'volunteered in the experiment, and were', 'rights, and are', 'TO YOU, AND SUCH'.
- Sentence-final '.' after legal, terms-of-service or methods sentences ('...changes to our website.', '...measurements.', '...pain is reproduced.', '...characterized.').
- ';' in license boilerplate ('Free Software Foundation;').
- 'of' in fixed frames: 'types of', 'professor of'.
- Action verbs that open a procedure step: 'start', 'begin', 'Start LinkManager', 'Deny', 'Allow'.
- Title words inside role phrases: 'principal' (investigator), 'Chief' (of Protocol / Financial Officer).
Weaker activity appears at ',', 'which', 'once', 'then' and 'where' that introduce the next clause.
expl.negative_pole:
Sparse and idiosyncratic, mostly in boilerplate or technical text.
- Strongest: the word 'for' in the Wikia notice 'We have a modified experience for viewers using ad blockers' (≈ -9). In that notice, 'using' ≈ -2, '!\n' ≈ -1 to -2, and 'experience' and '-to' are mildly positive (+1).
- Odd name fragments, e.g. 'omed' in Iomedae (-9), 'utt' in Guttormsson (-4).
- Newlines or periods ending a patent claim or software-doc paragraph before a new numbered or instruction line (-8).
- ':"' before a pasted log line (-8), 'Message:' (-5).
- 'when' in a definitional sentence ('pressure in arteries when your heart beats', -8).
- ',' in ad copy ('each month, you'll get', -8).
- Also milder: ':\n' before a bulleted list (-4), and '.\n' or '.' ending an expository paragraph (-2 to -3).
expl.rubric:
Background is 0; the vast majority of tokens fall below |0.5|.

Positive values:
- +6 to +10: clause-joining ', and' / 'AND' in legal or scientific sentences; a sentence-final '.' closing a terms-of-service, legal or methods sentence; ';' in license text; 'of' in 'types of' or 'professor of'; procedural verbs 'start' or 'begin'; 'principal' before 'investigator'.
- +2 to +5: ',', 'which', 'then', 'once' or 'any' near such junctions; 'Chief' in titles; '\n' after headings in policy text.
- +1: scattered function words ('the', 'by', 'is', 'to') in legal or procedural boilerplate.

Negative values:
- -8 to -9: 'for' in the Wikia 'modified experience for viewers' notice; certain line breaks or colons in patents, logs and docs; 'when' in definitions.
- -2 to -5: nearby punctuation, ':' before lists, odd name subword tokens.
- -1: many content words and prepositions in ordinary prose.

What does NOT fire it: ordinary narrative or marketing prose gets ~0 to ±1, even at commas and periods. The strong positive values need a formal, legalistic or stepwise-procedural register.

expl.label: Negative: function words in industrial/commodity production prose; weak positive: name-onsets, problem words
expl.positive_pole: Weak and scattered, usually +1 to +4. Two main triggers. (1) The first subword of an unusual or foreign surname or name: 'Sh' in Shuchman (+4), 'Sh' in Shaildabek (+3), 'Orb' in Orbistondo (+3), 'Qu' in Arquitectos (+3), 'Ish', 'Rash', 'Freme', 'Poll' (+1 to +2). (2) Nouns for problems, hazards or failures: 'fault' (+3), 'hazard' (+3), 'problem' (+3), 'problems', 'impurity', 'loss', 'pollution', 'resistance', 'adverse', 'earthquake' (+1 to +3). Also fires on 'answer' or 'database' in crossword-clue boilerplate (+4/+1). In technical result sentences ('experimental results show that') it gives a low, spread +1 to +2.
expl.negative_pole: The dominant pole. It fires in business or industrial prose about producing, processing, buying or trading raw materials and commodities: iron ore, crude oil, steel byproducts, pulp and paper, minerals, factory production lines, manufacturer marketing copy. The activation sits mostly on function words that link to a material or product noun, especially 'of', then 'and', 'to', 'for', 'a', 'the' and commas. Examples: 'facilitate usage of(-10) low(-5)-grade(-5) iron ore(-4)'; 'tonnes of(-8) iron ore'; 'at $US45.73 a(-6)'; 'buyer of(-5) West African crude'; 'inventory of(-5) light oil'; 'the production(-5) line'; 'raw(-3) materials(-4) and(-5)'. Descriptors of the material ('low-grade', 'high-quality', 'raw', 'balanced commodity') and words like 'production', 'ore' or 'materials' also go negative (-2 to -5). Within such a passage, many nearby tokens drift to -1 to -3.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for almost all tokens; random prose with no commodity or industrial content stays at 0. Negative values: in commodity, mining, manufacturing or trade text, 'of' or 'and' just before a material or product noun phrase gets -4 to -10. 'of' in quantity-of-commodity phrases ('tonnes of', 'buyer of', 'usage of') is the most extreme. Material adjectives and nouns get -2 to -5. Other tokens in these passages get -1 to -3. Generic corporate or financial text (margins, exchange rates, shipments) reaches about -1 to -4. Positive values: the first subword of a rare foreign surname gets +2 to +4, and later pieces of the same name +1. Problem or hazard nouns get +1 to +3. Ordinary common names and everyday words get 0. The neuron rarely exceeds |3| outside dense raw-material production text.

expl.label: Sparse: mid-identifier tokens in code, model numbers, names, boilerplate
expl.positive_pole: Tokens sitting partway through a structured, highly predictable identifier or template, where the continuation is nearly forced. The strongest case is the '.lang' in Java fully-qualified types such as 'java.lang.String' or '(java.lang.Exception' (about +10). Other examples: the ' <' that opens a placeholder in command-usage syntax ('-Mailbox <mailbox name>', +9); the first digit of a product model number ('Quiet Comfort 35' → '3', +7); boilerplate UI words on video sites ('Favorite; Report', +7); the first subword of an unusual personal or place name ('Naj|ee', 'An|neh|urst', 'De|B|arge', 'Per|mac|ulture', 'J|esse', 4–6); templated encyclopedia phrasing ('Their natural habitats are subtropical', with 'habitats' +6); URL path separators ('youtube.com/channel/', +5); the opening quote in 'category "Jewelry'; digits inside phone numbers, years and form IDs (+4–5); and the dot or digit inside version numbers or IPs ('5.1.1', '192.168.1.10', about +3).
expl.negative_pole: Also on tokens inside structured or templated strings, but in different templates. Examples: locants and fragments in IUPAC chemical names ('1-(3-ch...', 3 and -ch about -7); hotel-policy boilerplate ('Extra-person charges may apply', with 'charges' -6); reporter first names in Reuters bylines ('Reporting by ... and Julie Gordon', -5); the digit in a gene name ('p53', -5); metadata table labels ('Contact details of provider', -5); digits in exam or product codes ('000-132', -5); area-code digits in phone numbers (-2 to -4); engine specs ('2.0L', -4); and some prepositions inside fixed titles ('Picnic at Hanging Rock', 'Institute for Research', -4).
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 on almost all tokens: only about 0.1% of tokens reach |1|, so ordinary prose should be predicted as 0. Assign non-zero values only inside code identifiers, part/model/phone/version numbers, URLs, rare proper names, and boilerplate templates such as site UI text, product metadata, bylines and hotel policies. Within these, the activation sits on a middle token: a namespace segment, separator, first digit, or first subword of a name, not usually the final token.
- +8 to +10: 'java.lang' in Java signatures; '<' placeholders in command syntax.
- +4 to +7: model-number digits, rare-name subwords, UI boilerplate words, URL slashes, template nouns like 'habitats'.
- +1 to +3: version-number dots, ICD codes, labels like 'Genre:'.
- -3 to -7: chemical-name locants, Reuters byline first names, 'charges' in hotel policies, gene digits (p53), metadata labels like 'provider', certification-code digits, phone area codes.
Sign is hard to predict by surface form. Code namespaces, product models and UI/name subwords lean positive; chemistry, biology, byline and policy boilerplate lean negative. When unsure inside such a string, predict a small value of ±1–2.

expl.label: Year's final digit in metadata dates (+); error/message-introducing words (−)
expl.positive_pole: Digits of a year in a date stamp or metadata field such as 'Date:', 'Posted on', 'Uploaded:', 'Issue Date:', 'last updated on', or a publication year in parentheses. The peak falls on the last digit of the 4-digit year (the '4' in 2004, the '2' in 2022). The preceding year digits get small activations (+1 to +2). The hyphen or slash right after the year gets +2 to +4, and the following month digits get about +1. The effect is strongest in ISO-style YYYY-MM-DD dates that follow a label. Day or month tokens get weaker activation: '5/5 (Sunday, 16 December' gives +3, 'Oct' gives +3, and a leading '04-' gives +3.
expl.negative_pole: Tokens that set up a report of an error or message, typical of tech-support and forum text. Examples: 'get/getting an error', 'ends in a timeout', 'throws me a', 'fails with the message', 'result in an', 'Mysql::Error:', 'contains the following messages:', '会遇到', 'NOTE:'. The strongest values (−6 to −9) fall on the verb and the article or preposition just before the error noun ('get', 'an', 'in', 'a', 'with'). Opening quotes, colons, and newlines right before the quoted error text also reach −5 to −9. The error noun itself gets about −5, and words like 'says', 'message', and 'warning' get −3 to −5. Sentence-final periods or newlines at the end of notices and warnings (shopping-cart notices, RubyGems notes) can reach −5 to −8.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for almost all tokens.

Positive values:
- Last digit of a year in a labeled date or timestamp: +5 to +10 (+8 to +10 for 'Date: 2004-', 'updated on 2022/', 'Creation Date: 2016-').
- Last digit of a parenthetical citation year, e.g. '(…Ltd., 2013)': about +6.
- Bare years in prose, e.g. 'Sunday, November 27th, 2011': only +1 to +3.
- Earlier year digits: +1 to +2.
- Separator after the year: +2 to +4.
- Following month or day digits: about +1.
- Weekday, day, or month names inside a posted-on date: +1 to +3.
- Numbers that are not dates (prices, IDs, gallon counts): at most about +1 to +2. This includes something like '10 gallon'.

Negative values:
- 'get / an / a / in / with' immediately introducing an error, timeout, or message: −6 to −9.
- Opening quote or colon before the quoted error text: −5 to −9.
- 'error' / 'Error': −2 to −6.
- Weaker cues ('get a warning', 'freeze up with', 'fix many problems'): −2 to −4.
- Ordinary text with no error context: 0.

expl.label: Sparse; fires inside fixed boilerplate phrases and rare-name word fragments
expl.positive_pole: Mid-phrase tokens of memorized multiword expressions or names, where the continuation is highly predictable. Examples: "Agree with manuscript results **and** conclusions" (+7); the middle subword of unusual proper names such as Faval|ora, Mont|el|iro, Mont|el|ukast, Gram|mer, Rip|ley, Rip|off Report, Wink|el|nk|em|per; "Centre **of** Excellence"; "Ligue **des** droits"; "Leo **di** Caprio". Also website-UI and policy boilerplate: "Privacy & Cookies Policy↵N|ecessary", "By screening submissions, **we**", "you may set **your** browser", "keyboard shortcuts**:**", "navigate to login.↵", "dialog window**.**".
expl.negative_pole: The same kinds of contexts, with a different set of phrases. Financial and legal disclaimers: "Management's Discussion and Analysis of **Financial**" (-10, the strongest), "Analysis **of**" (-4), "registered trademarks **of** their respective owners" (-5), "actual results **may** vary" (-4). Copyright lines: "Copyright **©** 2018" (-4). Site-navigation menus: "Main Navigation," (-3 to -4). Fixed titles: "Picture **of** the Day", "Journal of Cosmetics, Dermatological **Science**". Registry IDs: "NL**4**149" (-6). Name fragments: Gen|o Smith (-5), P|io, Pan|aj|achel, Crist|ob|al, Giov|annon|i, Vickie Win|ans, "Musee **des** Beaux-Arts".
expl.rubric:
Default is 0 for almost every token. Only about 0.06% of tokens reach |1|, and almost none exceed |5|. Ordinary prose stays at 0.

Flag a token only if it sits in the middle of a stereotyped fixed string. Such strings include legal/financial disclaimers, copyright and trademark notices, cookie/comment/privacy policies, site navigation and login prompts, author-contribution statements, and journal or institution names. The other trigger is the inner subword piece of an uncommon multi-token proper name.

Magnitude by case:
- Typical hits: ±1 to ±3.
- Strong hits: ±4 to ±7, on a key function word (of/and/des/di/with) or a name-internal piece.
- Extremes: ±10, e.g. "Financial" in MD&A, -10.

The sign is phrase-specific and hard to predict:
- Lean negative for SEC, financial, copyright and trademark legalese, "X of the Y" titles, and navigation menus.
- Lean positive for cookie/privacy/comment-moderation UI text, scientific author statements ("results and conclusions"), and celebrity or brand name fragments (Mont-el, Rip-, Gram-).

Adjacent tokens in the same phrase can flip sign, e.g. "with" -5 followed by "and" +7. Common words outside such fixed frames do not fire.

expl.label: Templated web boilerplate and brand names (+); fixed scriptural/instructional phrases (−)
expl.positive_pole: Tokens inside templated web boilerplate and inside brand or product names, especially in lists. Examples: e-commerce platform lists (Op|enc|art, Os|commerce, 3|dc|art, OpenCart™ is a trademark of Open|Cart); forum footers ('Powered by vBulletin', with the peak on ' by'); forum post timestamps (' PM' after a time like 02:38); copyright year ranges (2000 - 2016); freelancer-marketplace spam ('5 freelancers están/estão ofertando'); stock privacy and contact lines ('functionality of our website', 'get back to you', 'accessible to any and all users'); file sizes ('31KB'); counts such as '404 Facebook Shares'. Also fires on mid-word subword pieces of uncommon proper names (Sum|it|omo, Emmy|l|ou, Str|atos, St|rel|ka, mambo-develop|er).
expl.negative_pole: Function words and continuations inside highly formulaic phrases in religious prose and step-by-step technical instructions. The strongest hits are prepositions and articles after a fixed head. Examples: 'take away the sins of' (take −7, of −7); 'Chechen Islamic Cultural' (Islamic −7); 'the goodness of the Lord' (goodness −5); 'Africa Cup of' (of −4). Instruction examples: '.htaccess file, located in the directory' (in −4); 'Deny from' (from −5); 'Order threads in' (in −5); 'File Manager' in cPanel instructions (−4); 'in the search box' (the −4). Also the newline right after 'View Single Post' (−6) or after a forum username (−4), and code fragments like '->select()->' (−4).
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for almost all tokens; about 0.3% of tokens reach |value| ≥ 1. Positive values: +6 to +10 on the climactic token of boilerplate or brand lists ('3' in 3dcart, ' Open' in 'trademark of OpenCart', ' by' in 'Powered by', ' PM' in a post timestamp, final year digit in a copyright range, 'ancers'/'están' in freelancer spam). +2 to +5 on neighbouring tokens in the same templated span: commas between list items, 'Version', '™', 'GMT', 'Views', 'is', 'representatives'. +1 to +2 on scattered pieces of rare proper nouns and on digits in templated numbers. Negative values: −4 to −7 on prepositions, articles or nouns in fixed scriptural phrases or tech-support instructions, and on the newline after 'View Single Post'. −1 to −3 on surrounding words in those same passages. Ordinary news, sports or essay prose stays near 0, even when it contains brands or numbers, unless the text is a templated footer or list.

expl.label: Negative: bond/rates/fixed-income finance jargon; weak positive misc tokens
expl.positive_pole: Weak and diffuse (rarely above +3). It fires on scattered tokens: 'per' in 'interest rate of 292% per year'; mid-word pieces of unusual names ('Dob' in Dobri/Dobelle, 'Tit' in Titmuss, 'ob' in Gobry, 'azz' in Gazzaniga); code/package syntax ('add', 'PackageReference', '-' in cmdlet parameters); and citation or catalog digits ('5' in 2257, ',' after a series number, 'uls' in Pulsar). There is no strong concept here; treat it as noise-level, +1 to +2.
expl.negative_pole: Strong. It fires on text about debt/fixed-income markets and interest rates, such as bond yields, spreads, swaps, Treasuries, repo rates, wholesale money markets, mortgage-backed securities, Fed rate policy, CD APY figures and bond coupons. Activation is spread over many consecutive tokens in such passages. The biggest values sit on the key jargon or on the function word that sets up the next technical term: 'money' in 'wholesale money markets', ';'/'the'/'on' in 'Interest rates also fell; the yield on the', 'over' in '120bp over mid-swaps', 'repo', 'Treasury', 'yields on', 'fed funds'. Numbers inside bond and rate quotes also go negative ('10Y', '850m', '6.5% 2041', '1.90% APY').
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for almost all text, including general news, everyday finance mentions and code.

Negative values, inside dense bond/rate/credit-market prose:
- Most tokens: -1 to -4.
- Core terms and their lead-in function words: -5 to -10. Examples: 'money' before 'markets' -10; 'over' in a spread quote -10; 'repo' -8/-9; 'Treasury' -8; 'yield on the' about -9; maturity/size digits in bond quotes -3 to -9.
- A brief mention, such as 'mortgage-backed securities' in a lawsuit story, gives -3 to -6.
- A loose finance context, such as 'interest rate of X% per year' in a payday-loan ad, gives about -1 to -2.
- Ordinary money talk outside debt markets stays near 0.

Positive values: assign +1 to +3 sparingly, only to these cases:
- 'per' after a rate percentage (+3);
- odd proper-name subword fragments (+2);
- package-manager/XML config tokens (+1 to +2);
- citation/series punctuation (+1 to +2).
Otherwise give 0.

expl.label: Sparse: operands in inline math/dimension expressions (+); name fragments, code digits (−)
expl.positive_pole: Mainly tokens inside inline arithmetic, formulas or dimension specs, especially the operand or number right after an operator or bracket. The strongest case (+10) is the final digit of a decimal inside a parenthesized multiplication, e.g. '(0.627 *'. Other examples: 'E' after '=' in 'P = I V cos(φ) = E V sin', '(' after '+' in '0.258 + (1-0.', 'z' in 'IQ = (z)(15)', digits and 'cm'/'x' in size specs like '224 cm x 32' or 'L 1970mm x W', and model-number digits like 'IT50EA'. A secondary weak cluster is mid-word subword pieces of uncommon proper names (Cr|ich|low, Gh|ass|ali, Sol|om|oni, Ologbosere, Sh|urm|ur, S|azer|ac), around +3 to +5. Also occasional +2 to +5 on discourse-starting tokens after boilerplate ('Here's', 'Also,' after an ad line) and in boilerplate disclaimers ('for your', 'and should').
expl.negative_pole: Weak, up to about −4. Fires on mid-word subword pieces of unusual names that do not have the positive flavor (V|ay|ner, Kal|umuk, Kers|cher, Kh|and|allah, Latvian 'Zvaigžņu'), garbled Devanagari byte tokens, and middle digits in ISBNs or document codes ('97800|0|6210', 'AR 6|0|0-63'). It also fires on function tokens in legal or affiliate boilerplate: 'to' in 'designed to provide', 'ANY' in 'WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY', '?' in 'Are you a student?', and the ',' or '·' in newsletter or social-media widgets.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 on nearly all tokens; only about 0.06% of tokens reach |value|≥1. Assign values as follows:
- +6 to +10: a digit or operand right before or after an operator inside a parenthesized numeric computation, especially the last digit of a decimal followed by '*'.
- +3 to +5: a variable or operand after '=' or '+' in a formula, units or dimension numbers in size specs ('cm', 'x'), rare-name subword fragments, and 'Here's' or 'Also,' starting a new line after boilerplate.
- +1 to +2: surrounding digits and brackets in the same expression.
- −2 to −4: odd-name fragments of the second type, ISBN or document-code middle digits, legal/affiliate boilerplate function words, and non-Latin byte fragments.
- Plain prose, ordinary numbers (years, percentages) and lists: 0.

expl.label: Place-name modifiers (Old/E./N./Main/Lower) beginning street/locality names after addresses
expl.positive_pole: Fires on the first word of a proper place or street name, especially a modifier that opens a street, district, or area name. Strongest after a street number or a locative preposition (on/along/around the/in). Typical carriers are directional words like N, E., W, East, the period after 'E.', and modifiers like Old, Main, Lower, Upper. Examples: '157 N Old Carriage Road' (Old +10, N +5); 'located on 2145 Old Union Road' (Old +9); 'around the Old Course' (Old +9); '210 E. Grand' (E +7, '.' +9); '222 East Broadway' (East +8); 'Lower Nazareth Township' (Lower +6); 'Main Stage' (+7); 'the main street' (+7); 'Phuket's old neighbourhood' (+8); 'the old Town' and 'the old city wall' (+6–7). Street-number digits just before the name get +1 to +5 and rise toward the name. The preceding 'on/along/the' gets +1 to +3. Words after the modifier ('Road', 'Town', 'Township') get about +1 to +3. Weaker on generic 'main/city/town' in location contexts: 'main lounge' +3, 'city centre' +3, 'Denver West' +2, 'North Shore' +2.
expl.negative_pole: Weaker (min about -5). Appears in real-estate and property feature listings describing amenities and layout. Carriers are connective tokens: 'with', 'and', '&', 'of', 'for', commas, 'has', 'feature'. Also amenity nouns: 'parking', 'golf', 'pool', 'driveway'. Examples: 'garden with driveway and garage' (with -4, and -4); 'two levels of concrete parking' (of -5, parking -4); 'neighborhood with easy access' (with -5); 'complex has 24 hour security and private parking' (has -4, parking -4); a golf scorecard yardage list ' 2,' (-5). Words like 'Excellent', 'Accessible', 'ample' give -2 to -3.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for almost all tokens. +8 to +10: the modifier word or directional abbreviation (Old/N/E./East/W) starting a street or locality name right after a house number or 'on/along/around the'. +5 to +8: the same in slightly less address-like context (Main Stage, main street, old neighbourhood, Lower/Upper Town). +2 to +5: house-number digits before it, the period in 'E.', generic 'main/city/old' in place contexts. +1 to +2: prepositions or articles leading in, plus head nouns (Road, Ave, Township). The neuron fires on the modifier, not on the street name's core word: 'Union', 'Grand', 'Broadway' get only about +1. 'Old/main/new' in non-place senses ('old friend', 'main reason') gives about 0. Negative: in property or amenity listings, give -2 to -5 to connectives (with/and/&/of/for/has) and amenity nouns (parking, pool, golf, garage); other listing words get -1 to -2.

expl.label: Negative: time-span units in 'X years/weeks ago/earlier' narrative backstory
expl.positive_pole: Weak and diffuse, at most about +2. Small bumps appear on assorted tokens: odd name subword pieces (Vad-ap-alani, Therm-alt-ake, Menden-hall, Ke-ckley), 'Yes, add me', 'convinced', 'knew', 'online', and 'that' after 'felt'/'meant to her'. There is no clear single concept here.
expl.negative_pole: Fires on the time-unit noun of a past-time offset phrase, in narrative text where an event happened some span before the reference point. Typical forms are 'two years prior', 'eight years ago', 'a few weeks ago', 'less than two months earlier', 'just weeks before' and 'had been on a conference call earlier'. The strongest value lands on the unit word ('years', 'months', 'weeks'). It also fires on 'earlier' or 'in' when 'earlier' itself is the offset. Related spots also fire: past-perfect or reported-clause contexts that set up backstory, such as 'asked me what I was doing there' (peaking on 'doing'), 'had brought them in front of', 'grateful to be', 'right away', and 'came' in 'X came to'.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for nearly all tokens.

Negative pole (time offsets):
- Time unit followed by ago/earlier/prior/before, in past narrative: -6 to -9.
- Words leading into the span ('less than', 'had been', 'just') and the trailing ago/earlier: -1 to -5.
- 'what I was doing there': 'doing' about -10, 'was' -6, 'there' -4.
- 'had brought them in front of': -2 to -8.
- 'came' in narrative ('Jesus came to', 'rulers came to'): -3 to -4.
- 'right away', 'to be' after 'grateful': -5 to -6.
- Plain durations with no past offset ('for almost five years', 'cook 35 minutes'): only about -1 to -2, or 0.
- 'Twenty years later': about -3.

Positive pole:
- Rarely exceeds +2.
- Give +1 to +2 to scattered name subword pieces, 'Yes,' in signup boxes, and complement 'that' after 'felt' or 'meant to her'.
- Otherwise 0.

expl.label: Flowing instructional/descriptive prose in recipes and product copy, especially cooking-step continuations
expl.positive_pole: Running imperative or descriptive text in recipe method steps and retail product descriptions. The neuron builds up across a sentence and peaks on function words that continue an instruction, such as "to", "for", "and", "," and ".". Examples: "bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook al dente, according to" (+10 on "to"); "Cook shells according to package directions" (+8, +7); "Let stand 10 minutes"; "rest, covered for 10 minutes"; "Cool on cooling rack 20 minutes". In fashion and home copy: "roll up the sleeves for summer", "makes it a stylish choice", "will give your little one", "to dress things up", "that you can do everything" (+3 to +7).
expl.negative_pole: Concrete physical-placement or quantity details inside recipes and health or advice text. It fires on the preposition or article before a container or location, such as "into the", "in a separate", "place in shallow", "line a baking tray" and "preheat the oven" (-4 to -6). It also fires on ingredient-list numbers and quantities: "Yield 4 to 5 servings" (-6/-5), "1/2 cup", "Calories 50" and lists like "nuts and fresh fruits" (-5). First-person habit statements also trigger it, e.g. "I usually watch that I don't" (-9 on "watch"). So do imperative advice phrases with "your" + object, e.g. "check your spam folder" (-6) and "reducing your red meat" (-5).
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for most tokens; news, bios and narrative text stay near 0.

Recipe method text and product-marketing prose get a diffuse +1 to +3 across most tokens.

Go higher on connective tokens deep in an instruction. Give +5 to +10 to "to", "for", "and", "," and "." after verbs like cook, bring, boil, stand, rest or bake, or after a time phrase. The biggest values come when the instruction continues a cooking process: "according to", "to a boil.", "for 10". In product copy, give +4 to +7 to "for", "that", "will", "it" and "to" in benefit or styling phrases.

Negative values go on tokens introducing a container or destination ("into", "in a", "the" before pan/bowl/dish/oven): -3 to -6. Numbers in ingredient lists or yields get -1 to -6, and fractions and "cup" get -1 to -3. Personal-habit or advice clauses get -3 to -9.

Recipe text can flip sign: process and timing continuations are positive, while placement, vessel and measurement tokens are negative.

expl.label: Product/tool/technology benefit claims: 'X can/will save time, make life easier'
expl.positive_pole: Promotional statements that a tool, product, system or technology gives the user a benefit such as saving time, money or labor, making life or a workflow easier, simplifying tasks, or adding convenience. The activation builds across the claim. It is highest on the modal or verb right after the tool's name ('plugins can', 'Google Maps has', 'appliance will', 'tools take', 'it would be', 'TheraOffice has been') and on the benefit noun or verb itself ('time', 'labor', 'life', 'workflow', 'conveniences', 'simplifies', 'expediency', 'Eliminate'). The tool's noun ('systems', 'tools', 'appliance', 'buttons') is also moderately active.
expl.negative_pole: Weaker and scattered. Mostly UI or shortcut menu terms ('Quick Access', 'Quick...', 'Instantly', 'ready-to-serve', 'such as' inside a feature list) and some name pieces ('Ranveer', 'OpenCart Limited'). Also hits phrases about sparing the user effort ('so you don't have to', 'I don't need', 'you're a click away'), plus the opening '(' or '“' in technical or software text. Typical values are -2 to -6.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for almost all tokens, including ordinary news, religious, travel and narrative text.

Positive values:
- +7 to +10: the key benefit word in an efficiency claim about a product ('offer time,' → time +10; 'make your life' → life +9; 'take your workflow' → workflow +9; 'plugins can' → can +9; 'conveniences' +8; 'time saving' → time +8).
- +4 to +7: modal or verb after a product or tech subject ('will', 'can', 'has', 'would be'), plus 'labor', 'simplifies', 'definitely help'.
- +1 to +4: the product noun and surrounding words in the claim ('systems', 'tools', 'kitchen appliance', 'to', 'levels', 'easily').
- +1 to +3: weak mentions of software features or tools without a clear benefit claim.

No positive firing on plain descriptions of products without an efficiency or convenience framing.

Negative values:
- -3 to -6: 'Quick' in UI menu names, 'Instantly', 'such as' in feature lists, 'so you don't have to' / 'I don't need', and the odd name subword.

expl.label: + final token of specific named kinds; − spatial prepositions/connectors after verbs
expl.positive_pole: The final subword/token that completes a specific named entity or kind-name, especially a taxonomic, genre, or product term: Metal|lica, sorgh|um, Ch|eddar, magn|olia, melanog|aster, marcesc|ens, apple (trees), Deep House, afro-be|at, pe|ony, pine, latex, cherry (gelato), Bieber, heavy rock, indoor (air), the closing quote after a song title (“7 Rings”). Possessives and quantifier/ordinal builds inside descriptive noun phrases also fire weakly to moderately: Norwegian’s international, Schroder's ... their share, first-ever. Typical magnitude is +3 to +6. Weaker spread of +1 to +2 falls on nearby determiners and modifiers (its, the, new, of).
expl.negative_pole: A preposition, or occasionally a conjunction or comma, that links a verb or noun of physical placement, motion, contact, or containment to a location or object NP.
