expl.positive_pole: Promotional or enthusiast lifestyle prose about food, wine, sake, art, crafts, fragrance, design or gifts. The activation lands on the connector or function token that sets up the next category noun: '&', 'and', ',', 'of', 'for', 'with', 'about', '/', '-made', '-course', '-based'. Examples: 'wine &| food', 'love for| beauty', 'world of| sake', 'jewelry,| glass,| pottery and| woodenware', 'passionate about| creating', 'wines and| spirits,| coffee', 'fill the bottles with| fresh flowers', 'Welcome fruit basket/| platter'. Adjectives just before the category noun also fire moderately ('regional', 'Puglian', 'favorite', 'remarkable', 'authentic', 'Vermont-made', 'fresh'). It fires most in a list or pairing of offerings or crafts, such as food & drink, art media, gift categories or cuisines.
expl.negative_pole: Specific product naming and descriptive detail in beauty/skincare reviews and yarn/textile listings. Tokens inside branded product names carry it: 'Supple Moisture Rich Silk Cream', 'Tinted Day Cream', 'NARS', 'MAC', 'Merino/Silk Ombre', 'Handicrafter Cotton Twists', '100% Pure Wool'. Texture or finish descriptors also do: 'dewy', 'chalky on the skin', 'looks like a cream'. So do 'every' in 'every bottle' and the items in 'from fresh juice to soymilk'. Magnitude is largest on the head words of a product name (−5 to −8); surrounding words in the same sentence sit around −1 to −4.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for almost all text; ordinary prose, technical and news text stay at 0 with occasional ±1. Positive scale: +8 to +10 for '&', 'and', ',', 'of' or 'for' linking or introducing food, drink, art or craft category nouns in enthusiastic marketing ('wine & food tours', '5-course harvest dinner', 'love for beauty'). +4 to +7 for adjectives or nouns completing such phrases, or for list commas between craft or product types. +1 to +3 for nearby function words in the same promotional passage. Negative scale: −5 to −8 on brand or product-name tokens and texture/finish words in cosmetics, skincare or yarn product descriptions. −1 to −4 for other tokens in those review sentences. What does NOT fire: the same domain nouns ('food', 'wine') in plain non-promotional text, and the category nouns themselves, which are often weaker than the connector before them.

expl.label: Injury narrative (+) vs. bones/joints health-anatomy context (−)
expl.positive_pole: Fires inside acute-injury reports, mostly sports news, on the function words just before the injured body part or injury noun. Typical frames are 'out/forced off with a [strained] hamstring', 'after aggravating his strained right calf', 'injured his ankle', 'broke my leg', 'suffering a nasty gash', 'return from his hip issue' and 'must have been broken'. The peak lands on the determiner or possessive (a/his/my), on adjectives (strained, broken, sore, nasty) and on laterality words (right, left). It is weaker on with/after/from and on injury verbs. The injury noun itself (hamstring, concussion, leg) is usually low.
expl.negative_pole: Fires in health, anatomy or product text about bones, joints and muscles as things to protect, treat or move, rather than an individual's acute injury. The strongest spots are the preposition, conjunction or article just before 'joint/bone/muscle', as in 'glucosamine for bone & joint health' (the 'for' and '&' tokens), 'injected into the joint' (into/the), 'muscle and joint pain', 'my bones and joints', 'help bones and muscles develop', 'fold at the joints', 'cut off at the hip joint', 'surfaces of the facet joints', 'pain in the arms' and 'old bones'. It also extends weakly to similar frames about physical structures, e.g. 'cracks and weak points', 'bendable tail and…' on a toy figure, and 'major muscle groups'.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 on nearly all tokens; the neuron is silent outside body and injury talk. Positive values: +3 to +5 on 'a/his/my' or on adjectives like 'broken', 'strained' and 'right' when they directly precede the injured part in a sports or personal injury report. Give +2 to 'with', 'after' or 'from' starting the injury phrase, and +1 to injury verbs ('injured', 'tearing', 'broke') and to the body-part noun. Clinical phrasing ('treating patients with RCT') gets about +2 to +3. Negative values: -5 to -10 on 'for', '&', 'and', 'into' or 'the' right before bone/joint/muscle in wellness, supplement, medical-treatment or anatomy text ('for bone & joint health' gives -8 and -10). Give -3 to -5 for 'at the joints', 'of the facet joints' and 'bones and muscles', and -1 to -2 on surrounding exercise or chiropractic text ('align the', 'your knee should'). Mixed medical passages can show both signs. Anatomy words in non-body senses (city names, clothing hips) get at most ±1.

expl.label: Sparse proper-name onset neuron: (+) place-name/address starts, (−) mid-name or acronym pieces
expl.positive_pole: Fires on the first token (often a subword fragment) of a proper name, especially a place or street name in an address or location list, where the model must predict how the name continues. Typical cases: 'Cal' in Calle / Calabasas / Calhoun / Calvary (+6 to +8); 'W' and especially '.' in street addresses like '100 W. Imperial Highway' or '1501 W. Badger Rd.' (+4 to +7); 'Stone' in 'of Stone[ Mountain]', 'Saint' in 'Saint John', 'west' in 'west LA' (+4 to +5); 'BUCHAREST' (+5). It also fires on opening fragments of foreign surnames and titles ('Mur' and 'avs' in Muravschi, 'Cap' in Capriccio, 'Mal'/'ac' in Malacca, 'z' in Amzulescu) and on the '(' that opens a parenthetical name or country code ('(Lohengrin)', '(BA)') at +1 to +3. There are rarer weak hits inside formulaic multi-token phrases ('of' in 'flask of ointment of pure', 'correct' in 'how to correct material', 'or' in a medical list), and occasional digits in dates or DOIs.
expl.negative_pole: Similarly sparse. It fires on tokens inside foreign or unusual named entities and acronyms, typically after the name has begun or at an acronym or code piece. Examples: 'ar' in Harput within a Turkish city chain (−10); 'P' in 'Iohannis – PNL' with '–' at −6 and 'Justice' at −5; 'ana' and '0' in 'Ultimasaptamana: 0' (−7, −8); 'i' in 'i5' (−7); 'O' in 'OAO' (−6); 'Maj' in Majd (−5). Other examples: 'Cad'/'and' in 'Cadence and Magma' (−4), 'al' in 'albanian' (−4), 'Required' in 'Required fields' (−5), 'special' in 'special services', 'Common' in 'Common Cranes', and 'Jim'/'George'/'Oakland' at −2 to −4. Romanian, Russian, Turkish and Albanian contexts are common, as are capitalized modifiers before a head noun.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 on nearly all tokens; under 0.2% of tokens reach |1|. Ordinary prose, function words and common words give 0. Assign +5 to +8 to the first token or prefix fragment of a place or street name in an address or location list ('Cal'abasas, 'Cal'le, 'W'+'.' in a street address, 'Saint' John). Assign +2 to +5 to the onset of foreign surnames or titles and to direction words before place names ('west LA'). Assign +1 to +3 to '(' before a bracketed name or code, and to the commas between names in cast lists. Assign −4 to −10 to the interior or acronym pieces of foreign or political names and product codes ('Har'+'ar'put, 'PNL', 'i5', 'OAO', 'Ultimasaptamana' pieces). Assign −2 to −5 to capitalized modifiers or first names that precede a known head ('Required fields', 'Common Cranes', 'Jim Comey', 'Oakland University'). Within a single name, signs can alternate across subwords, e.g. 'Am' +1, 'z' +5, 'ules' −4. When unsure, predict 0.

expl.label: Church/liturgical context: function words before specific names (+) vs. saintly enumerations (−)
expl.positive_pole: Mostly in Christian church, liturgy or parish-bulletin text. It fires on function words and connectors that come right before a specific named item, place, event or term. Typical triggers are 'the', 'of', 'on', ':', opening quotes, and the first digit of a year or time. Examples: 'back down the center aisle to the [street end] of the' (the +7, of +2, the +5); 'Holy Eucharist, Rite II: A festive celebration… using the more contemporary language of' (+3 to +6); 'officially called "E[vangelii]' (" +3, E +4); 'known as the “sede vacante”' (+3); 'on the first Saturday of November' (the +5); 'celebrate the Res[urrection]' (+4); 'from 3:30 to 5:00' (the 0 in 5:00 gets +5); 'Page 4 June 13, 2005' (the space before 2005 gets +6). It also fires weakly on church-adjacent formal text such as addresses, product names, and ceremony programs ('playing of "Taps"').
expl.negative_pole: Mostly in Catholic or devotional text. It fires on descriptive, quantifying or evaluative words about saints, virtues, sacraments or religious life. The strongest case is a number that counts a sacred enumeration: 'the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit' (seven −10, then of/the −4). Other examples: 'seven demons' −3; 'Veronica was a pious woman' (pious −5); 'The Blessed' −4; 'lived a perfect life without sin' (without −4); 'live your commitment' (your −4); 'the saint's other accomplishments' (−3); '244 Catholic colleges' (−3). Weaker cases appear outside religion: list or comparison words such as 'alongside' in a crypto article (−4), and bullet dashes in a probiotic ingredient list (−2 to −3).
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for nearly all tokens; |value| ≥ 1 occurs on only about 0.1% of tokens. Outside religious or church text, predict 0 except for rare ±1–3 on date digits, list dashes, or comparison words.

Within church/liturgy text:
- 'the', 'of', ':' or an opening quote directly before a named liturgical rite, place, season or document: +2 to +7.
- The first digit of a time or year in a church schedule: +3 to +6.
- Surrounding function words such as 'and', 'on', 'a': +1 to +2.
- Content nouns themselves are usually 0 to +2.

Negative values:
- A number counting sacred things ('seven gifts'): −3 to −10.
- Adjectives of sanctity ('pious', 'Blessed') and 'without sin'-type phrases: −3 to −5.
- Possessives or 'other' about saints, and 'your' in vocational exhortation: −2 to −4.
- Ecclesiastical nouns like 'Catholic', 'Vatican', 'Deacons' in news prose: about −1.

expl.label: Subword pieces of English-context proper names (+) vs. foreign-language word pieces (−)
expl.positive_pole: Tokens inside multi-token proper names in English text: the first subword or an early subword of a rare surname, place name or institution name (Luc|ado, Wilbur-E|ll|is, S|yc|amore, Pur|dy, Rose R|og|ers, Sm|oltz, Lued|ers, Lake Bl|uff, W|adi, Roy|se City, Cam|arillo, Om|agh, Kam|men, Hol|ubeck). The neuron also fires on words partway through official named titles: National Health «Interview» Survey, Library of Congress «Catalog»uing, «the» Canada Fitness Survey, House «of» Representatives, Children«’s» Alliance, Administrator «Pamela» S«.» Hyde, skew-T / «log». It fires most strongly when the token is mid-name and the name is not yet complete or predictable. One outlier: a Turkish legal title (Kişisel Veriler«in» Korunması Kanunu) gave +6.
expl.negative_pole: Subword pieces of non-English words, especially Turkish, Polish, Welsh, Danish, Norwegian and transliterated Slavic text. Examples: aydınlat«ma» −10; Naj«le»«ps»«zy» −5 to −9; Nant«-y» −6; Personalhistor«isk» −5; Zazn«acz»«ono» −5; uyar«ınca» −4. Weaker negatives (−2 to −5) fall on parts of descriptive or technical compound noun phrases: white-«l»ipped peccary, «jumping» jack, «live» AIS ship tracking, «cast» wheels, Inmarsat«-»4, the digits of dates such as 2016 in a leap-second notice, and (O)eWF acronym pieces.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for almost all tokens; ordinary English prose and common words stay at 0. Positive values: +4 to +6 for an early subword of a rare surname or place name in English text, or a key word in the middle of an official program, survey or catalog title. +2 to +3 for function words or initials inside such names ('of', 'the', 'S.') and for the first piece of less-rare names. +1 for familiar or adjacent name pieces, such as celebrity names (Carm|elo, St|oud|emire) or the first word of a list of place names. Once a name is completed and predictable, its later pieces drop to about 0. Negative values: −5 to −10 for inner or suffix subwords of foreign-language (non-English) words, with the largest values on Turkish and Polish suffixes. −1 to −2 for other tokens in that foreign stretch, which may alternate with small positives. −2 to −5 for modifier tokens within English technical or descriptive compound noun phrases and for list item separators or digits in technical lists. Fewer than 0.2% of tokens reach |value| ≥ 1.

expl.label: Sparse polysemantic neuron on mid-name and mid-term tokens in proper nouns and jargon
expl.positive_pole: Positive values appear on a token in the middle of a multi-token proper noun, brand, or technical term, where the model has started an entity and must continue it. The examples are scattered and share no topic. Mid-word cases: Yu-G(i-Oh), (l-m)onom(ethionine), Hy(drate), Techn(ol), Am(ish), Gl(encore), Gl(anz), Trib(l)end, Bro(es), First(Rand), t(undra), gl(immer), /G(HGs), and (Fried)reich's at(axia). It also fires on connective tokens inside fixed formulaic phrases: '2 and 20', 'Skills and Experience', 'Sciences and Engineering', 'title, author', 'informational purposes only', and 'ID number'. A third group is name or start-of-entity tokens: Jay, Red-(Headed), and the bloggers in 'KidLit bloggers'.
expl.negative_pole: Negative values also fall inside names, titles, and rare terms. The strongest is the title word 'Secretary' in 'Treasury Secretary William McAdoo' (-10). Other examples: rare technical nouns (sty(lobate), tal(us), sw(amps)), mid-syllables of foreign place names (Ş-eb-inkarah), brand or site suffixes (LibraryThing, PRWEB, ASSA ABLOY), title or role words (Dame, Fort King, Domestic), mid-surname pieces (Fab-ry), the 'at' in 'Picnic at Hanging Rock', 'Data' in 'Social Science Data Archive', and nuts-and-b(olts). Some cases are near-duplicates of positive ones, so the sign is hard to predict.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for nearly all tokens; only about 0.3% of tokens reach |value| ≥ 1. Ordinary prose, function words, and numbers in normal text stay at 0. Positive rules: assign +3 to +5 to a token inside a multi-token proper noun or technical term, usually the 2nd–3rd subword or the first token after a capital fragment (Gl|encore, Hy|drate, Techn|ol). Give +3 to +4 to 'and' or a comma inside fixed bureaucratic or listing phrases ('Skills and Experience', 'Sciences and Engineering', 'purposes only'). Give +1 to the neighbors of these tokens. Negative rules: give -4 to -6 to rare technical nouns or foreign-name syllables (stylobate, talus, swamps, Şebinkarah). Give -3 to -5 to brand or site name pieces (LibraryThing, PRWEB, ABLOY) and to a title or honorific placed right before a person's name. Give up to -10 for a government-office title word ('Secretary' after 'Treasury') preceding a name. Give -1 to adjacent surname fragments and commas in author lists. If unsure, predict 0; the effect is rare and either sign is possible inside names.

expl.label: Function words in flowing prose and formulaic slots (+); Title-Case headings and names (−)
expl.positive_pole: A dense, low-level positive signal on ordinary running prose, mostly function words and punctuation: the, a, of, with, commas, and, his, your, this. It peaks on the token just before a highly predictable continuation in a formulaic slot. Peak examples: the day-of-week token starting a date line after a mailing-list or email signature (".eu\n" → "Mon" +10; "winehq.org\n" → "Thu" +10). Also the leading "2" of a year in a date ("October 2021" +7, "Apr 26, 2011" +7, "(2009)" +7), and the field value right after a forum label ("Join Date:" +7, "seen|" +9). Within narrative prose, peaks fall on the determiner or verb before an expected noun: "hit the| floor" +8, "wrong side of the|" +8, "on your| keyboard" +7, "the whole prairie catches|" +7, "That reportedly included|" +8. Repeated parallel descriptive lists also peak, e.g. "a white with silver stripes" (silver +9).
expl.negative_pole: Content tokens inside Title-Case headings, product or service listings, and multi-token proper names or technical terms, often word-internal pieces. Examples: "D|Phil" −8; "Laser Vag|inal" −6; "Inade|qu|ately" −6; "Making The Decision To Undergo Vasectomy" ("go" −5); "Methods of| Losing Water Weight" −5; "Neighborhoods Act|ively Prepare" −5; "N|uestra" −5; "El| Segundo" −5; "Akashic Records/Psychic" −4 to −5; "Thor|acic" −4; "Div|ina" −5; a bullet "*" starting a list item −5. Explicit-content captions in Title Case also go negative.
expl.rubric: Background: in ordinary prose, most function words and commas sit around +1 to +3, with about a quarter of tokens ≥1. Content nouns are usually about 0 to +1, sometimes −1. Assign +4 to +6 to determiners, articles and verbs in vivid narrative or descriptive sentences just before a strongly expected noun. Assign +7 to +10 to formulaic slot openers: weekday or month after an email or URL signature line, a year's first digit in a date, a value after a "label:" or "|" field, and "the" before a stereotyped noun such as floor or side. Assign 0 to −2 to proper-noun pieces in plain sentences. Assign −3 to −8 to word-internal or capitalized tokens in Title-Case headlines, menus, taglines, service lists, degree abbreviations, or foreign or medical multi-token words; bullets that start a list item can also reach about −5. URLs and identifiers themselves stay small (about +1 to +3); the peak lands on the token after the line break that begins the date.

expl.label: Late characters inside random alphanumeric/hex/numeric strings (+); mid-word rare-name fragments (−)
expl.positive_pole: Tokens deep inside opaque, non-word character strings such as URL shortener IDs (pic.twitter.com/1yWMWWGT3q, amzn.to/2GSkbNv, ift.tt/1G7Kd7X, goo.gl/eh0Ua), YouTube video IDs, hex colors (#ecea26), IPv6 addresses, dimension strings (1280x1024, 300x75), codes (T48.3X5S, 280E), and version or part numbers. The activation lands on a single digit or letter chunk several characters into the string, usually near its end, after the model has seen enough of it to know it is gibberish or alphanumeric. Digits within numeric runs (the 0 in 1280x, 240v) are typical carriers.
expl.negative_pole: The second or third subword piece of an unusual proper name, username, or rare word when the model is completing or recognizing a previously seen name rather than reading random characters. Examples: almot|ri|ptan (-6), j|inx|nit55 (-5/-4), Fc|ON|SiX (-5), k|1|Ng0r (-5), Gle|am|Tech (-5/-3), d|re|amees (-5), z|ill (-3/-4), Qu|ir|ky (-3/-4), Q|uby (-4), Horn|wood (-4), Wich|ans|ky (-3). This is strongest on a repeated mention of a name seen earlier in the text.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for almost all normal prose tokens. Inside random IDs, hashes, hex codes, or numeric dimension strings, give +1 to most characters and +3 to +6 to the one or two peak tokens near the end of the string; give up to +10 for a clearly random Twitter/shortener ID late in the string. Early characters of such strings, and separators like '/', '://', '=', can be 0 or -1. Ordinary numbers in prose (years, prices) get 0, with a small +1 to +3 at most for multipliers like '3x' or times like '2 P'. For rare names, brand fragments, or usernames being re-spelled from context, give -2 to -6 to the inner subword piece, typically the 2nd piece; the first piece gets about -1 or -2. Common words and well-known names get 0.

expl.label: Chemistry/materials technical text: formulas, compound names, composition lists
expl.positive_pole: Tokens inside technical chemistry or materials-science prose. This covers chemical formulas (RuCl2(PPh3)3, Na2O, Cu + 3 H2), peptide or compound name fragments (Boc-Pro-ΔPhe), product or material names (Austral exflam, borosilicate, acrylate), and ingredient or composition lists (polyacrylate base, sodium chloride, purified water). It also covers measurement and spec strings (m/z 91, 107; 10-milliliter) and the connective words in such text (of, with, and, using, in). Activation builds over the passage. It peaks on mid-word subword fragments and on formula closers like ')', '2', '.' in dense chemical runs. A lone token ' then' at the start of a clipped fragment can also hit +8.
expl.negative_pole: Sharp, isolated dips on specific science-word tokens, mostly the prefix or first piece of a compound term. Examples: 'micro' -3 / '-' -8 in micro-organisms, 'bio' -4/-5 (biofilm, biofuel, bio-row), 'carbon' -3/-4 in 'carbon dioxide', 'ethylene' -4, 'angiotens' -4, '-' in physico-chemistry -5. Also ', ' separators in all-caps keyword lists (-3 to -5) and 'immuno' -5. In ordinary narrative or news text there is a mild -1 background on many tokens.
expl.rubric: Background in non-technical text is 0 to -1; casual prose hovers around -1 on scattered tokens. In general scientific or technical prose, assign +1 to +3 on most tokens, including function words. In dense chemistry, formula, or materials-composition passages, assign +4 to +7. Peak values of +8 to +10 go on formula pieces (')', subscript digits), rare chemical or brand fragments ('fl' in exflam, 'il' in borosilicate/milliliter), and spec numbers late in the run. Product, spec, or ingredient lists outside strict chemistry (water bottles, lamp specs, essential-oil recipes) get +2 to +5. Within the same technical passage, prefix tokens of compound terms ('bio', 'micro-', 'carbon' before dioxide, 'immuno', 'ethylene') flip to -3 to -8. Commas in uppercase keyword indices get -3 to -5. Pure biology or medical prose is mixed: mostly +1 to +3, with these negative dips on such tokens.

expl.label: + first subword of split rare words; − day digits in dates, name fragments
expl.positive_pole: Weak, modest activations (+3 to +5) on the first subword fragment of a word the tokenizer breaks into pieces. Examples: 'cro' in crores, 'kn' in knoll/knotted/knitted/knobby, 'clo' in cloths, 'competit' in competitively, 'elig', 'chang' in changelog, 'Alg' in Algarme/Algocida, 'bulld' in bulldozer, 'N' in Nino, 'Lib' in Libby, 'Care' in CareFirst. The neuron seems to be predicting the word's continuation. In sports text it also fires on 'the' (+3) in phrases like 'in the', 'begin the', 'winning the' before a conference or tournament name (Pac-12, Big 12, NCAA), and on 'in' (+2) in those same phrases.
expl.negative_pole: Strong. The main trigger is the digits of the day number inside dates: 'September 2|2', 'August 1|2th', '2010-02-0|5', '2013-07-2|5', 'Jul 2|6', 'May 2|0|1|4'. The digit token that begins or forms the day gets about −7 to −10, and year digits sometimes get −2 to −7. A space token right before a day number ('October ␣23') also gets about −4 to −6. A secondary trigger is fragments of brand, company or proper names, often foreign: N|ortel −7, Mo|eller −6, Su|ja −6, FX −6, non-K|eny −6, Saf|ar|icom −2, Ar|tha −3. Location and venue contexts get weaker values (−1 to −3), such as the Big 12 name itself (−1 to −3) and '-seat'.
expl.rubric: Background on almost all tokens is 0. Day digits inside dates: −7 to −10. Year digits in dates: −2 to −7. A space before a date number: −4 to −6. The first subword of a split proper name or brand: −2 to −7. Conference names (Big, Pac, -12) and 'overall' in records: about −1. First fragment of an ordinary or rare English word split mid-word (kn-, clo-, competit-, cro-, elig-): +3 to +5. 'the' after 'in', 'to' or 'winning' in collegiate sports contexts: +3, with 'in' at about +2. Do not fire on whole common words, or on plain numbers outside dates (prices, stats get ~0 or −1).

expl.label: Predicts upcoming 'log': + for word-internal fragment (c|logged), − for standalone log/login
expl.positive_pole: Fires on the token immediately BEFORE an expected word-internal 'log'/'logs' fragment, i.e. when the current token is a prefix that 'log' will complete. Examples: 'c' before 'logged' or 'logs' (+10, +5), 'web' before 'logs' (+9), 'back' before 'logs' (+7), 'CO' before 'LOGNE' (+5), 'PHARMACO' before 'LOGY' (+4). It also fires on similar ambiguous word-starting fragments that could continue that way, such as 'sp' in spammers/spidery (+6/+7), '-c' in self-cleaning (+5), '|c' in cottage (+6), 'Techn' (+5), 'R' in Rival (+5) and '-s' in foot-soldiers (+5). The activation sits on the prefix token, not on 'log' itself; 'log' itself is only about +1.
expl.negative_pole: Fires on the token BEFORE an expected standalone word 'log', 'login', 'log in', 'log out', 'logging', 'changelog' or 'Logos' in computing or account contexts. This is usually a verb slot: '->' before 'log out' (−7), 'must' before 'log it' (−5), 'to' or 'you' before 'login'/'Log In'/'Access' (−4 to −5), 'server' or 'audit' before 'log' (−3/−4), 'chang' before 'elog/elist' (−3/−4), 'Channel' before 'Logos' (−4). Weaker negatives (−1 to −3) appear on nearby function words in login/password/account instructions ('to', 'you', 'could', 'still').
expl.rubric: Background is 0. A diffuse +1 to +2 is common on content and function words in descriptive, list-like or legal prose (e.g. 'and', ',', 'service marks', 'organized'); occasionally this reaches +3 to +5 on coordinating 'and' or list tokens ('both physically and', 'trademarks,'). Strong positive (+5 to +10): a short word-start fragment or compound prefix whose likely continuation is the subword 'log(s/ged/ne/y)', e.g. c→logged, web→logs, back→logs. Other ambiguous fragments like 'sp' or 'c' score about +5 to +7. Strong negative (−3 to −7): the token right before a standalone 'log'/'login'/'log out'/'log file' word in tech or account contexts, especially after '->', modal verbs ('must log'), 'to', 'you' or 'server'. Tokens that are themselves 'log' or 'logged' score only about +1. Ordinary text with no log prediction scores 0.

expl.label: Predicts upcoming locative 'there' (negative); diffuse positive pole
expl.positive_pole: Diffuse and only weakly coherent; typically +2 to +5, rarely up to +10. Two recurring groups. (1) Words in goal/motion or transfer phrases just before a destination or complement: 'help us' (+5 on 'us'), 'Get' in 'Way to Get Pitchers', 'Before I get emails', 'get your supplies where', 'transferring files between', 'Lead You To', 'move us in', 'be fully recovered', 'Twitter right HERE'. (2) Early pieces of capitalized names or brands: GE Monogram, GEAB, Stax, Oswalt, Hussey, US-ACAN, Gulf Marine, Eve's, Urban Outfitters, Mall Artha, 'Tie a Yellow Ribbon', and 'detailed information' (+7). Weak +1 to +2 also appears on ordinary content nouns ('traffic', 'resources', 'humidity') and on 'be', 'are', 'is' inside predicates.
expl.negative_pole:
Strong and clean. It fires on the token immediately BEFORE the adverb 'there', i.e. where the model expects 'there' to come next.
- 'out' in 'out there' (-8 to -10): 'so much content is out there', 'providers out there', 'any of you out there'. It still fires when the next word is something else, as in 'what's out on the market' (-8).
- Verbs or copulas followed by locative 'there' (-8 to -9): 'I was there', 'it is there', 'still live there', 'help us get there'.
- Commas or connectives that may introduce existential 'there' (-3 to -8): 'That said,' then 'there are…'; 'In addition,'; 'Nonetheless,'; 'After mass,'; 'Besides X,'. Also 'While' (-4) in 'While I was there'.
The 'there' token itself is NOT active.
expl.rubric:
Background is ~0; most tokens fall in -1 to +1. Many function words, especially infinitival 'to', sit at about -1.
Negative values:
- -8 to -10: 'out' in 'out there'; a verb or copula just before locative 'there' ('was/is/live/get' + there).
- -3 to -8: a sentence-initial discourse comma or connective likely to be followed by 'there are' or a new clause.
- -1 to -3: weaker anticipations of this kind.
Positive values:
- +3 to +7: an object pronoun or noun after 'help/get/lead' in goal phrases ('us', 'you', 'supplies', 'files'); 'get/GET' starting a motion phrase; 'fully' or 'be' in 'be fully recovered'; the first subword of brand or proper names (GE, Stax, Osw, Hus).
- +1 to +2: generic content nouns and predicate 'be/are/is'.
Do not put the activation on 'there' itself. Do not fire negative on 'there' meaning 'their', or when 'there' is unlikely.

expl.label: Negative: token right before 'water' (predicting 'water'); weak positive misc.
expl.positive_pole: Weak and diffuse, at most about +3. It fires on mid-word or name-continuation tokens: 'P|ric' in PricewaterhouseCoopers/Priceline, 'Hilary D|uff', 'Gal|lo', 'Spark|America'. It also fires on 'well' before a hyphenated participle (well-run, well-supplied, well-placed). Treat it as mostly noise-level.
expl.negative_pole: The dominant pole. It fires on the token immediately BEFORE the word 'water', when context makes 'water' the likely next word. Examples: 'could you please [water] me', 'food and [water]', 'conserving [water]', 'warm, ill-tasting [water]', 'hot bottled [water]', 'in [water]', 'bath[water]', 'pool and spa [water]', 'drinking [water]', 'cold [water]', 'Losing [Water Weight]', 'pot|able [water]'. The value lands on the predicting token, not on 'water' itself. 'water' and the token after it are near 0. Weaker spillover appears on earlier tokens in water-themed phrases ('Knowing about conserv...', 'Practically all the'). It also extends to close cousins such as 'land and [underwater]' and 'Living [Dream]' in Waterwalker context.
expl.rubric:
Background on nearly all tokens is 0.

Negative values:
- Token directly preceding 'water' when that next word is strongly predictable from collocation or context (food and, conserving, hot/cold/warm, bottled, drinking, pool, bath, please [water me]): -5 to -10.
- Same position but 'water' is less certain, e.g. after prepositions like 'in'/'of' in a water-topic text: -2 to -5.
- Other tokens a few positions earlier in water-centric sentences, and punctuation near them: -1 to -3.
- The token 'water' itself: about 0.
- Mentions of other liquids without a water expectation: 0.

Positive values:
- Mid-name pieces like 'ric' in PricewaterhouseCoopers/Priceline: +1 to +3.
- 'D' in Duff: about +3.
- 'well' before a hyphenated or adjectival participle: +1 to +2.
- Occasional list items, e.g. 'Soccer': up to about +2.
- Otherwise 0.

expl.label: Mid-word fragments anticipating an '-it' continuation; sign set by the expected ending
expl.positive_pole: A word-initial or word-internal subword fragment whose most likely continuation is a short word ending such as 'its', 'ito' or 'ite', usually in rare, compound or loan words. Examples: armp|its, crankba|its, spinnerba|its, affidav|its, sgraff|ito, bur|ito, pleb|isc|ite, Sol|itaire, nitty-gr|itties. Weaker cases complete a word with a similar stem-final fragment: conce|aling, dece|iving, gl|owed, spray-p|ainted, take aw|ays, end|ometrial, hors|eshoes, rem|anded, non-ch|lorine, brow|ner, d|EB. The activation sits on the fragment token just before the predicted ending, not on the ending itself.
expl.negative_pole: The same kind of fragment token, but where the expected continuation is 'it' followed by a longer Latinate suffix chain ('-itable', '-ited', '-itician', '-itarian', '-itously', '-iting', '-itting', '-ithecus', '-it' as in merit/pundit). Examples: hosp|itable (-5), aud|ited (-5 to -3), -pol|itician / pol|itics (-5 to -4), Author|itarian (-5), precip|itously (-7), Austral|op|ithecus (-5), jan|itresses (-5), P|und|it (-4), relaxed-f|itting (-4), inc|iting (-3), Mer|it (-3). Also: Can|aan (-5) and Devanagari/Sanskrit fragment bytes (-10 in an Indic transliteration list).
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 on almost all tokens. Whole common words, spaces, punctuation and word-final tokens stay at 0. Only mid-word subword fragments activate.

Positive values:
- Fragment predicting plural 'its' or the endings 'ito'/'ite'/'itaire' in a rare word: +4 to +8 (armpits +8, affidavits +4, sgraffito +4 to +5, plebiscite +4).
- Fragments completing other uncommon words (conce|aling, deceiving, nitty-gritties, endometrial): +2 to +6.
- Weak fragments in brand names or loanwords (Off-B|roadway, lim|o, Gl|itter): +1 to +2.
- The following 'it' token itself is sometimes slightly positive (+1 to +2).

Negative values:
- Fragment before '-it' plus a longer suffix (hospitable, audited, politician, authoritarian, precipitously, australopithecine, janitresses): -3 to -7.
- Indic script byte fragments: up to -10.

Sign heuristic: a short word-final '-its' or '-ito' ending means positive; '-it' + able/ed/ician/arian/ously/ing means negative.

Do not fire on ordinary common words tokenized whole.

expl.label: Neg: predicts upcoming 'aut-' (autism/autograph); pos: word-initial fragments awaiting completion
expl.positive_pole: Sparse, high values on the first piece of a word that the tokenizer has split, at the point where the model must supply a specific continuation piece. The activation sits on the opening fragment, not on the completion: 'sk' (skinned/skis/skews), 'be' (beading/BEINGS), '/ne' (neutered), 'K' (Kola), 'L' (Louboutin), 'H' (H&M), 'MON' (MONDAY), 'mon' (monamon), 'Garn' (Garni), 'N'/'endor' (Nendoroid). Often these are brand names, foreign words or ALL-CAPS text. A few whole-word cases where the next word is highly predictable also fire, e.g. 'LAST' before 'YEAR' (+10) and 'this' before 'year' (+3). Weak positives (+1 to +3) fall on assorted function tokens: '(', '-', newline before a list item, and '1' starting a year such as 1961.
expl.negative_pole: Fires on the token right before the model expects the next token to begin with 'aut-' (autism, autograph, autonomous, aeronautics). Strongest is 'with' in 'people with [autism]' (-10). Other examples: 'sign/signing' before autographs (-5), 'as' before autonomous (-5), 'aeron' before 'autics' (-7). In autism-organization text (e.g. 'Autism Speaks'), sentence boundaries and newlines that might be followed by 'Autism' reach -6 to -8, and so do words like 'get', 'reach', 'What:'. Similar contexts that might lead to 'special needs' or a named condition give milder values (-2 to -4) on 'with', 'in', 'that', 'as'.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for almost every token; only about 0.1% of tokens exceed |1|. Negative values: score -8 to -10 for 'with' after 'people/children/patients' in disability or autism text where 'autism' is the likely next word. Score -5 to -7 for a token directly before a likely 'autograph'/'autonomous'/'-autics' continuation. Score -2 to -6 for punctuation, newlines and verbs inside autism-charity pages. Small -1 values appear scattered on digits and other tokens. Positive values: score +6 to +10 for the opening subword fragment of a split word that has a determined completion (sk, be, K, L, H, MON, /ne), especially in brand names, product terms or caps text, and for 'LAST' before YEAR. Score +2 to +5 for similar but weaker fragments, a year-initial '1', or '(' and '-' before a predictable continuation. Do not fire on the completion piece itself (e.g. 'ut', 'oub', 'DAY' are about 0 or -1). Ordinary whole words get about 0. The word 'autism' itself is not strongly active; the activation lands on the token before it.

expl.label: Predicts upcoming 'alternative/option/substitute' noun; negative on superlative/genre-category descriptors
expl.positive_pole: Tokens that come right before an expected word like 'alternative', 'option', 'substitute', 'choice', 'version', 'solution' or 'way'. These are mostly the adjective or determiner slot in front of that noun: 'a sensible [alternative]', 'humane [alternative]', 'cheaper [alternatives]', 'a good [substitute]', 'low-cost [options]', 'open-source [distribution]', 'The subsequent [choice]', 'debt-relief [alternatives]', 'as an [alternative]'. Also fires on 'search for [alternative]', 'look for new [markets]', and 'The [alternative]' after an alternative has been mentioned. The surrounding context is about replacing something: cheaper, better or different options, a turn to something else, or comparing choices.
expl.negative_pole: Tokens inside descriptive category or superlative phrases that set up a genre, industry or ranking noun. Examples: 'one of the biggest [law firms] in [Cyprus]', 'the largest debut funds in the growth company segment', 'most popular philosophy show in the world' (with 'in' and 'the' around -4 to -5), 'the American punk', 'pop punk', 'adult power ballads', 'Top Ten Articles'. Also fires on some proper-name or rare-word starts: 'Cor|inne' -7, 'chees|ecloth' -6, 'Tr|icubes' -5. Values are typically -2 to -7.
expl.rubric: Background is about 0 on almost all tokens. +8 to +10: an evaluative adjective or determiner directly before an expected 'alternative' in clear substitution context ('humane', 'sensible', 'a ideal for', 'for' in 'search for alternative tests', 'The' contrasting with an alternative). +5 to +7: cost or quality adjectives in an option context ('cheaper', 'low-cost', 'good substitute', 'more recent version', 'open-source'), 'as an' before an alternative role, 'describe'/'compare' in method comparisons. +2 to +4: weaker setup tokens ('a', 'are', 'perhaps', 'than any', 'turning to', 'Or,', 'Another'). The word 'alternative' itself usually gets about 0. Negative: -3 to -6 on 'in'/'the'/genre adjectives inside superlative or category descriptions, and -5 to -7 on odd name-fragment tokens. Mild -1 is common on preceding function words in descriptive sentences. Ordinary text not about options or categories stays at 0.

expl.label: First token of rare proper names (+) vs. first subword of ordinary multi-token words (−)
expl.positive_pole: Fires on the first token of an unfamiliar, foreign, or rare proper noun, where the name is split into several subword pieces. This covers place names (Uherce, Sevier, Delden, Yichang, N'Djamena, Seine), surnames (Cawley, Misi, Mladin, Scicluna, Rottensteiner), brands and labels (Sealy, Thistle, Threeman, YTO), institutions (Maitreya, Sera Jey, Scrovegni), and Latin species names (Prostratus). The activation sits on that initial piece, typically a capital letter or capitalized fragment such as «U», «C», «Se», «Sc», «D», «M», «Th». Later pieces of the name get little or nothing.
expl.negative_pole: Fires on the first subword piece of an ordinary lowercase English common word that is split into pieces, where the model has to finish a known word. Examples are «l»ull, «l»ighthearted, «l»uster, anti-«de»pressants, ever-«d»ynamic, «hy»dropower, self-«e»vident, «unin»formed, un«ap»ologetic, well-«o»iled, «Gr»atitude, and acronym starts like «A»IOps. A few rare proper-name starts are also negative, e.g. «De» Pere around -9 and «L»aver around -3. There is also a diffuse weak negative, about -1 to -4, on function words and verbs in fluent, abstract or self-help prose (to, a, the, your, is, of).
expl.rubric: Background: most tokens sit at 0 to ±1. Running prose has frequent small negatives of -1 to -3 on function words, especially in motivational or explanatory text. Positive scale: first piece of a rare foreign or proper name, mid-text in a list, biography or address context, gets +6 to +10. Moderately familiar names or brands get +3 to +5 (Baltimore, Cajun, E3, Mugs). Capitalized words that are common and single-token get about 0 to +1. Negative scale: first subword of an uncommon common word being completed gets -8 to -10, on the piece right before the predictable continuation. Mild cases get -3 to -5. Do NOT fire positive on common names or whole-word tokens, or on the 2nd and later pieces of a name. The 2nd and later pieces of common words are usually about -1.

expl.label: Onsets of foreign/proper-name words (+) vs. memorized fixed phrases and elisions (−)
expl.positive_pole: The first subword of a capitalized proper name or foreign-language (mostly Romance) word that is split into several tokens and appears inside or near English text. The activation sits on the opening fragment, before the rest of the word is known: « L»lorar, « K»avala, « B»ologna, « K»immel, « F»oulonne, « Be»aux-Arts, Car«ref»our, « E»umetra, Le«M»ieux, M«ille» Miglia, « B»ence. Some Spanish, Portuguese and French suffixes or function words also fire mildly: Investig«ación», Conserv«ación», « Lors», « des», « en», « droits». A capitalized all-caps word starting a line does too: «P»UBLISHED, «P»ARGO. Typical values are +1 to +4. Nothing in these examples went above about +4.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for almost all tokens. Ordinary English prose and common English names stay near 0.

Positive values:
- +2 to +4: the first fragment of an unfamiliar multi-token foreign or proper name embedded in English; the strongest cases are Romance names or words.
- +1 to +3: Romance suffixes and particles (-ación, des, en, de) inside such names.
- About +1: weaker cases.

Negative values:
- −8 to −10: tokens deep inside verbatim web boilerplate (RePEc, Wikia ad-blocker notice) and the apostrophe in d'/D' elisions within names.
- −5 to −6: inner words of well-known titled names or events, and Lorem ipsum.
- −1 to −4: mid-word pieces of running non-English sentences.

The continuation token of a name (e.g. 'avala' after K) is usually near 0. Activations are very sparse: only about 0.07% of tokens reach |value| ≥ 1.

expl.label: Signed, alternating activity inside website boilerplate (ad-blocker, terms, disclaimers)
expl.positive_pole: Tokens in stock website/legal/meta boilerplate that lead into or name the specific content of the formula, typically just before or on the payload phrase. Examples: " using" in "for viewers using ad blockers" (+8 to +9), with " ad" +4 to +5 and " blockers" +6 right after; " to" in "using extensions to block ads" (+7); "descending"/" order" in forum sort instructions (+7); "ographic" in "bibliographic or download information" (+6); " intelligent" in a comment-moderation policy (+6); " embed" (+4); " style" in "with style sheets (CSS) enabled" (+4).
expl.negative_pole: Other tokens in the same kind of boilerplate, especially the following. 1) Modal or negated auxiliaries in disclaimer and aphorism sentences: " may" in "any use which may be made" (-10), " must" (-9), " cannot" (-6). 2) Head nouns or verbs that close a clause and set up the next predicate: " site" in "Wikia is a free-to-use site that" (-7 to -9), " contact" in "...information, contact" (-9), " update" in "Cannot delete or update a parent row" (-8). 3) Subject+verb starts: " have" in "We have a modified experience" (-6 to -7), " from"/" advertising" (-3 to -4), " you" (-3 to -7), and a comma before "we provide" (-9). Milder negatives of -1 to -5 show up on licensing, cookie, signup and company-blurb text.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for almost all ordinary prose (narrative, recipes, news, technical text); only about 0.1% of tokens reach |1|. Only predict activity when the text is formulaic site or meta boilerplate: ad-blocker notices (the Wikia template is canonical), cookie/privacy notices, terms or comment policies, 'contact us for corrections' notes, EU funding disclaimers, 'be the first to review', 'sign up for newsletter', CC licenses, forum UI help, corporate 'About X' blurbs. Inside such text, most tokens take small mixed values of ±1 to ±3. Large values follow this pattern: about -8 on the noun that names the site/entity before a relative clause or predicate; about -6 to -10 on modals and negations (may, must, cannot, will) and on 'We have'/'you are' openers; about +6 to +9 on the preposition or participle that introduces the key specific object ('using' → ad blockers, 'to' → block) and on the object words themselves (+4 to +6). Within one template the magnitudes are consistent: the Wikia notice gives site -9, from -4, have -7, using +8, blockers +6. Isolated odd tokens inside names, such as 'Marvel'ous, B'Tselem 'se', 'Gaud'ium, or M/E/A/N, can give +3 to +4. Do not fire on generic uses of the same words ('using', 'site', 'may') in normal prose.

expl.label: Website boilerplate/template text (ads, forums, footers); sign flips by token
expl.positive_pole: Positive values come from content words in generic website chrome and boilerplate. Examples: ad-blocker notices ('disabling these ads|+10 blocker'), word-list/anagram pages ('in this word|+7 list'), H-Net notices ('submitted|+7 to us'), and forum or vBulletin footers ('Copyright', '-' in '2000 - 2016', 'vBulletin|+6'). Others: 'emailed to me|+6', 'this site has|+5 to offer', '24/7', 'Then|+5 you can start reading', 'Publisher:', 'members' in 'users browsing this thread', and 'other marks|+4 are trademarks'. The activation usually lands on the noun or verb completing a stock phrase: ads, word, submitted, me, has, Embed, bold.
expl.negative_pole: Negative values come from digits inside dates and timestamps in forum post headers. Examples: '07-19-2003' (digits about -4 to -7), 'Posted 27 June 2003 - 04|-8:26 PM', and 'Apr 26, 2011'. Also negative are tokens in stock boilerplate that come just before the key word. Examples: 'up|-10-to-date web browser', 'Work Step by|-8 Step', 'Ad blocker interference detected|-5', 'for viewers|-5', 'further modifications|-6', 'custom ad blocker rule|-6', 'Version 3.8.7' (-2 to -3), and HTML tag lists ('<i|-6>'). Text ending 'ISO8859|-6' also goes negative.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for ordinary prose: news, articles and narrative never fire. Fire only inside web boilerplate.
- Ad-blocker notices: the closing object noun is +5 to +10 ('ads', 'blocker'). 'you'/'are'/'detected'/'viewers' are -3 to -5. 'you’ve' is +3 to +4.
- Word-list templates: 'word' before 'list' about +1 to +7, 'list' -3 to -4, 'Words' +1, 'adding one letter' -1 to -2, 'bold' +3 to +4.
- Footers: 'Copyright' +3, the dash in a year range +6, the final year digit -6, brand names +4 to +6.
- Forum and post dates/times: individual digits -2 to -8, strongest on the year's last digit and on the hour.
- Subscribe/sign-in and app-download prompts: the completing token is +5 ('me', 'has', 'Then').
- Metadata fields: 'Publisher:', 'Free*', 'credit card details' give +3 to +5.
- Elsewhere in boilerplate, small mixed values of ±1 to ±2 are common.
- Isolated proper-name fragments in lists ('Gur'ung, 'Kor'aput) can reach +4, but this is rare.

expl.label: Predicts the next word will be "default" (settings or debt sense)
expl.positive_pole:
Fires on the token immediately BEFORE a likely occurrence of the word "default". The activation reflects a prediction about the next word, not the word "default" itself.

Software/settings sense:
- "accept the| default name" (peak +10 on "the")
- sentence-initial "By| default" (+5–6)
- "-by| default"
- "the| default character format"
- "for| default character formats"
- "switch the input mode from the| normal…"
- "the system's| video"
- "set ones preferred| default"
- "which has a| recommended size"
- "menu items … would get| [default]"
- "used to define| user preferences"

Financial sense:
- "If the debtor falls behind or| fails" → "or" (+4), since the expected continuation is "defaults"
- "the United States to| go off"
- "avoid a government| shutdown"

Neuroscience sense: "connectivity between the| anterior…" (default mode network).

The neuron fires on the prediction even when the actual next word turns out to be different.
expl.negative_pole: Negligible. The most negative value is about -0.7, e.g. "By| screening", where "By" did not lead to "default".
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 on almost all tokens.

By how strongly "default" is expected as the next word:
- Very strongly expected ("accept the ___", "click to restore the ___"): +7 to +10 on the determiner or preposition right before it.
- Sentence-initial "By" in technical or how-to text: +4 to +6.
- "or"/"to" in debt contexts where "default" is a plausible verb ("falls behind or", "the US to"): +2 to +4.
- Settings contexts where "default/standard/recommended" is plausible next ("from the", "has a", "set the", "would get"): +1 to +4.
- Weak settings or preferences context ("changed the| username", "change their| preferences"): about +1.

The word "default" itself, and the tokens after it, get about 0.

"By" or "the" in contexts where "default" is implausible gets about 0, or slightly negative (≥ -1).

expl.label: Word-start fragments of split words (+) vs. Spanish name-opening articles (−)
expl.positive_pole: The first subword piece of a word the tokenizer splits into several pieces, where the rest of the word is still to come. Short consonant-initial stubs fire most: «t», «T», «-t», «br», «fl», «Gr», «z», «lo», «le», «c», «iz», «av». Clothing and textile words are especially strong: tassel, tights, tunic, taffeta, tummy, high-tops, lace-t(rim), brim, bracelets, bracing. Also fires on pieces inside Spanish or other foreign words and names in English text (z|orro, V|iz|c|aya, prim|av|era, le|ch|on, H|uet, D|á|vila, Ob|ispo, jard|ines). Separately, it gives moderate positives on some function and content words inside Spanish sentences: «español» +7, «de» +7, «disponible» +8, «ya» +4, «para» +5.
expl.negative_pole: Spanish (and Filipino-Spanish) proper names embedded in English or Spanish text, with the activation on the opening token of the name. Strongest on articles and possessives that begin a name: «La», «Los», «Las», «El», «Nuestra», «del», «de la», «dela». Also strong on the first piece of a Spanish surname or place name after a first name or title: «S»ánchez -9, «P»ampa -4, «Tep» -6, «Com»edor -6, «B»ú -6, «N»ueva -6. Examples: «La» Hosteria -8, «La» guerra -10, «N»uestra Salud -10, Mar «del» Plata -1. Later pieces of the same name can flip slightly positive (+1 to +3).
expl.rubric: Background is 0 on almost all tokens; ordinary English text is 0. Positive side: a word-initial fragment that is clearly incomplete, especially in a clothing or textile word, gets +4 to +8 (lace«-t» +8, «t»assel +5, «T»unic +5, high«-t»ops +6, «br»im +5). Fragments inside foreign or Spanish words and names get +2 to +8 (Nueva V-iz-«c»aya +5, «z»orro +8). Words inside a Spanish sentence embedded in English get +2 to +8 (de +7, disponible +8). Other first fragments of rare multi-token English words get +1 to +3 (glitz +2, Infirmary +3, Revol +2). Whole, common, single-token English words get 0. Negative side: the article or first token that opens a Spanish proper name (restaurant, book, organization, place, surname) gets -4 to -10 (La/Los/El/Nuestra -6 to -10). A connecting «de», «del» or «la» inside such a name gets -2 to -7. Spanish-text tokens like «su», «libro», «¿Qué» can get -4. A comma right before a Spanish name gets -1 to -6.

expl.label: Fragments inside rare multi-token names and words; boilerplate phrase tokens positive
expl.positive_pole: Fires on an early sub-word piece of an unusual proper name or foreign word, where the model must commit to completing a specific memorized name. Typical tokens: the first capital piece or a hyphen-joined piece. Examples: 'V' in La Venta and Rincón de la Viejá, '-D' in Scooby-Doo, 'Am' in Amrou and Amalia, 'Tro' in Trooper, '-X' in Jávea-Xàbia, 'sol' in solohsu, 'Rob' in Robidas, 'P' in Pannu, 'De' in Dean & DeLuca, 'M' in Mute Swan, 'Reb' in Rebney, 'Rev' in Revit. It also fires on the middle tokens of fixed, memorized multiword names and website boilerplate. Examples: 'and' / 'Consumer' / 'Street' in the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act; 'Support' in My Oracle Support; 'Public' in View Public Profile; 'is' in 'This is an older thread'; 'or' in 'Pagination or Media Count'; 'resolve' / 'over' in 'a 6ya expert can help you resolve that issue over the phone'; 'Member' in Silver Member.
expl.negative_pole: Fires on very similar contexts: a word-initial or word-internal fragment of a rare name, foreign word, or brand, usually 1–3 characters. Examples: 'ef' in Lefkada (-10), 'N' in Nazeer (-9), 'Tw' in Twila and Twinkies (-7/-6), 'b' in bolognese, 'ob' in photobooks, 'af' in Øyafestivalen, 'Ton' in Tonaci, 'N' in Nutter, 'Ver' in Verilerin, 'Ish' in Ishikawa, 'iy' in Kiyomori, 'Ph' in Phuket, 'sn' in snocross, 'Kan' in Kanban. The negative side is more often a mid-word piece of a single long word (Asian, Turkish or Greek names, place names, brand names). It is less often part of a boilerplate phrase.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for almost all tokens: ordinary English words, punctuation, numbers, and the final pieces of names. Only consider nonzero values on the first or middle sub-word token of an unfamiliar proper noun or foreign word, or on a token inside a well-known fixed phrase or interface boilerplate. Usually only one token per name is strongly active, and it is the early fragment, not the completion. Sign is hard to predict, so use these heuristics. Lean negative (-3 to -10) for short fragments inside long foreign or brand words: Greek, Turkish, Japanese, Indian names; food or brand coinages like Twinkies and bolognese. Lean positive (+3 to +7) when the fragment is a capitalized initial piece, the piece after a hyphen in a compound name (Scooby-Doo, Jávea-Xàbia), or a familiar Western or Spanish name. Give boilerplate or fixed-phrase internal tokens +2 to +5. Neighboring tokens in the same name often get small ±1–2 values of either sign. Typical strong values are ±5–7; ±10 is rare. Do NOT fire on common words, on full single-token names, or on the final completing piece of a name (e.g. 'oo' in Doo, 'kada' in Lefkada ≈ 0).

expl.label: Predicts the next token starts with 'pe'/'Pe' (pepper, peek, peptide, Pe-names)
expl.positive_pole: Fires on the token right BEFORE a token the model expects to begin with 'pe'/'Pe'/'PE' or 'pe'-like subword pieces. Typical continuations: pepper ('salt and|' → pepper, 'black|' → pepper), peek ('sneak|' → peek), peptide ('forms of|' → peptides, 'ply|' → peptide), peas ('can of|'), peat, PEIS ('Solar|'), pecker ('Wood|'), -peak ('Easy-S|'), and brand or person names already seen in the passage: PeepSo, Peppers, Peeters, Peet, Pepperdine, Peugeot, APEX. The activation sits on the predicting token (often a function word such as 'the', 'of', 'a', 'and', ',' or a newline, or a word-fragment), not on the 'pe' token itself. Magnitude is strongest when earlier context has already primed a specific Pe-word, e.g. a name repeated through the passage.
expl.negative_pole: Negligible. At most about -0.4, on scattered tokens such as phrases leading to 'easy'. Treat as 0.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 on almost all tokens; only about 0.03% of tokens reach |value| ≥ 1.

- **8–10:** A primed Pe-word is strongly expected next. Examples: 'Both the PeepSo Excerpt and| the|' before PeepSo; 'come across| a|' before 'plethora of pe…'; ', the|' before the Peppers foursome; 'Purafl|o' before 'peat'.
- **5–7:** Collocational predictions. Examples: 'sneak|' → peek; 'black|' → pepper; 'salt and|' → pepper; 'can of|' → peas/soup; sentence-final '.' or newline when the next sentence likely restarts with a recurring Pe-name; 'A|'+PEX; 'ply|'+peptide.
- **1–4:** Weaker or partial expectation. Examples: 'pe' word-pieces whose likely continuation is another pe-piece; tokens a few steps before the target, such as 'to the Draft' before 'Solar PEIS'; 'salt,|' in a spice list; 'Wood|'pecker on early mentions (~1–2), growing (~4) with repetition; 'Guadalu|'pe (~2); 'Delta P|' before 'he' (~2–5).
- **0:** The 'pe' token itself is usually only 0–3. Tokens following a pe-word are ~0 unless another 'pe' is anticipated.
- **Does NOT fire:** generic text with no imminent 'pe' continuation, or ordinary words that merely contain 'pe' mid-word without being predicted.

expl.label: Neg: plural 'countries/nations/cultures' predicted; Pos: mid-word rare subword pieces
expl.positive_pole: Weak and diffuse (max ~+4 in practice). It fires on the first or early subword fragment of a rare or foreign proper noun or uncommon word, where the model must commit to completing an unusual word: thr|ifty, ins|ipidus, Nig|uel, bes|pectacled, gren|ache, sant|alum, Mars|capone, Khaj|uraho, Igatp|uri, Thir|uvanmiyur, ens|ues, ing|ested, conce|aling, In|ca Kola, OeWF. One boilerplate case recurs: in the Wikia ad-blocker notice, 'from' gets +2, 'a' +1, and 'for' +4 to +5 in 'makes money from advertising. We have a modified experience for viewers'.
expl.negative_pole:
Strong. It fires on tokens immediately before an expected plural collective geographic or people noun such as 'countries', 'nations', 'cultures', 'populations', 'societies' or 'communities'. The modifier or quantity right before that noun peaks:
- 'Asian' in 'many Asian countries' (-9)
- 'developed' in 'developed countries' (-7)
- '0' in '60 countries' (-8)
- 'ing' in 'oil-exporting world' (-8)
- 'European' in 'European cultures' / 'European populations' (-5 to -7)
- 'American' in 'South American nations' (-7/-8)
- 'many' in 'in many countries' (-5)
- 'ο' in a homoglyph-spelled 'cοuntries' (-10)
Buildup words also go negative: 'in', 'the', 'than', 'more', 'other', 'these', 'among', and commas inside lists of peoples or leaders (-2 to -5). The noun 'countries' itself is usually only about -1. 'Oeuvres' after 'Negociants en' also reached -8.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for almost all tokens.

Negative values:
- -5 to -10: the adjective or number immediately preceding a predicted 'countries/nations/cultures/populations/societies' noun.
- -2 to -5: preceding function words and quantifiers in phrases like 'in more than 100 countries', 'among the peoples, leaders, and institutions' or 'other countries'.
- -1 to -3: 'different' or 'three different' before locations, and 'United' before 'Nations'.

Positive values:
- +3 to +4: an initial fragment of a rare, multi-token word or foreign place/product name, mid-word, before the completion. The word's first piece usually gets it; sometimes a later piece does (Igatp|uri).
- +1 to +2: other pieces of foreign names, e.g. 'Mekong', 'artemisinin', 'CasaBlanca'.
- +4 to +5: 'for' in the Wikia ad-blocker text.

Common words, ordinary prose, and code-like text stay at 0.

expl.label: Incomplete word-start subword fragments; sign set by fragment identity
expl.positive_pole: The first piece of a word that the tokenizer has split, where the word is clearly unfinished and the next token completes it. Only the fragment token itself fires. It is strongest (+7 to +10) for short onset fragments, especially 'Sp'/'sp' (Sp|okesman, Sp|andex, Sp|ots, Sp|oken, sp|areribs), 'R'/'r' (R|CT, r|ashes, r|uckus, R|abbi, R|icciardo, '/R'|SD) and 'sub'. Similar strength for onsets of rare names and loanwords: Sch|wenksville, L|huillier, Pel|angi, bur|rito, K'|Hor. Occasionally a whole word fires when it sits in an odd slot, such as 'The' at the start of a title ('The| Ides of March') or a sentence-initial 'By'. Mid values (+2 to +4) come from fragments like tor|rid, revol|ting, Be|iber, BE|ER, Am|miel, sp|idery and Display inside a URL.
expl.negative_pole: Also word-start fragments, but different ones. Typical triggers are consonant-cluster onsets with r or l ('tr', 'Tr', '/tr', 'br', '-br', 'contr', 'Kl', 'Clo', 'Amb') plus 'pres', 'beh', 'Em', 'Ar', 'Yan' and 'oly'. Examples: Kl|out (-10), rattle-tr|aps, Tr|ance, /tr|acker, contr|aband (-6 to -7), re-br|anded, pres|cribes, beh|eld, Em|igsville, Clo|stridium (-6). Weaker cases (-3 to -4): contr|asts, e-br|ake, Amb|roise, proteoly|tically, Ar|abic, Yan|acocha. A function word after an odd noun phrase can also go negative, e.g. 'with' in 'external engines with' (-6).
expl.rubric: Background is 0 for almost all tokens, including ordinary whole-word tokens and the completing (second or later) pieces of split words. Only consider tokens that begin a word and are visibly cut off, so the next token continues the same word. If the fragment is Sp/sp, R/r, sub, or the onset of an unusual proper noun or loanword (Sch, L, Pel, bur), assign +6 to +10. If it is a tr/br/contr/Kl/Cl-type cluster, or pres/beh/Em, assign -5 to -10, with Kl and contr strongest. For other unfinished fragments, assign small values of about ±1 to 3, with the sign uncertain. Leaning positive fits soft or descriptive words and names (torrid, revolting, Beiber); leaning negative fits technical or Latinate words (proteolytically, Arabic). Common words split into fragments usually stay below 1. Strong activations are rare, roughly 1 token in 3000.

expl.label: Word-initial subword fragments (esp. 'f'/'F') of multi-token words; sign varies by word type
expl.positive_pole: The first fragment of a word the tokenizer splits into pieces, usually an 'f'/'F' piece. It is strongest when that piece begins a descriptive modifier or participle, especially after prefixes like well-, pre-, re-, un-, fully, or touch-. Examples: 'fully F|enced' (+8), 'well-f|urnished' (+7), 'ref|inished' (+6), 'Pre-f|inished' (+5), 'unf|ertile', 'unf|urled', 'touch-f|riendliness', 'forced f|umbles', 'horse-d|rawn', 'well-f|itted' (+4). It also fires on some food words and names: 'F|udge', 'F|OMO', 'GeoF|USE', 'T|iberias', 'oak f|oudre', 'Meatball al F|orno', 'D|inosaur', 'D|MC'. Weaker cases (+1 to +3) include 'four-l|ane', 'f|ad diets', 'Fl|annelette', 'Ar|ario', 'SED|GHI', and some 'ex', 'y', 'Te' fragments.
expl.negative_pole: The same kind of fragment (again mostly 'f'/'F', also 'w', 'pe') when it begins a noun, proper name, or capitalized term. Examples: 'f|eral cat' (-10), 'Spear f|ishing' (-9), 'Dodd-F|rank' (-8), 'A-F|LEX', 'Wanted F|ugitives', 'bell w|ether', 'Fortune's F|avourites', 'San Mateo-F|oster City', 'pe|ccary', 'SMALL F|RIES', Swedish 'fram f|öra' (-7), '5-F|ive' (-6). Weaker cases (-3 to -5) include 'San Anselmo-F|airfax', 'Van F|ossen', 'F|-Cord', 'F|rette', 'turned-f|riends', and 'F|its all'. Hyphenated place and brand names are a strong negative cue.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 on almost every token, including ordinary whole-word tokens; only about 0.2% of tokens exceed |1|. Only the first subword fragment of a split word fires, and the following pieces stay near 0. That fragment is usually an 'f'/'F' piece, less often a short piece such as d, l, ex, y, T, D, Ar, w, or pe. Assign the sign this way: for a modifier or participle split after prefixes like well-/pre-/re-/un-/fully (fenced, furnished, finished, fitted, drawn, fertile), give +4 to +8. For a split proper name, title, brand, or noun, especially a hyphenated name (Dodd-Frank, Mateo-Foster, A-FLEX) or a word like feral, fishing, fugitives, or fries, give -3 to -10. Food words and foreign or common names are mixed but lean positive at +3 to +5. Rare diffuse +1 to +4 values appear on ordinary text such as numbers ('35,000') and 'from the burning of'. If the case is unclear, predict a magnitude of 2 to 4 and guess the sign from the word type.

expl.label: Word-initial subword fragments: lone S/s/N/n positive, b/f/j/Sp negative; comparison lists
expl.positive_pole: Mainly the first piece of a word that the tokenizer splits, when that piece is just the letter S or s (or N or n). Examples: 'S|emi-portable', 'S|avers', 'S|oul', 'Auto-S|cope', 'S|uck', 'non-s|ubsidized', 'S|unny', 'fence-s|itter', 'S|elenium', '*S|eltzer', 'N|INE', 'n|ixed', 'n|autical', '/s|ports'. These fire most when they start a new line or list item, or follow a hyphen or slash. A weaker second source is prose that compares attributes or lists benefits, often with high/low/less/more wording: 'switch to', 'such as', the commas in 'easier, faster', 'Lighter - Less', 'with much less', 'never goes above', 'range, extended'. In these, function words and list commas get +2 to +7.
expl.negative_pole: The first piece of a split word when it starts with other letters, especially b, f, j or 'Sp'. Examples: 'mid-b|ass', 'pre-f|inished', 'Sp|ree', '/J|. Scott', 'f|ends', 'j|owl', 'pref|olds', 'j|ingle', 'M|ondays'. These run about -3 to -6. Some content words in high/low or rise/fall contexts also go negative, each about -3 to -5: 'too' in 'too low', 'or' in 'raised or lowered', 'Cold' in 'Cold air drops', 'weather' in 'the weather turned', 'career' in 'career-high', 'keeps' rising.
expl.rubric:
Background is about 0. Almost all tokens sit below 0.5 in magnitude; only about 0.5% reach 1.

Positive values:
- A lone 'S' or 's' that opens a split word at the start of a line, list item, or hyphenated compound: +5 to +10. The top case is +10, for '-S|emi' after a dashed list.
- A lone 'N' or 'n' that opens a word: +5 to +6.
- 'and' inside a title such as 'The High and the Mighty': about +6.
- Connectors and commas in comparison or benefit lists ('to', 'such', ',', '-'): +2 to +7. Nearby 'with', 'a', 'at', 'and' in such lists: +1 to +3.

Negative values:
- A word-initial fragment starting with b, f, j, Sp, J or M, especially after a hyphen or slash: -3 to -6.
- Words of degree or change ('too', 'or', 'Cold', 'weather', 'career'): -3 to -5. Neighbouring tokens: -1 to -2.

Does NOT fire:
- Whole common words starting with s ('skies', 'some').
- An S that is a complete ordinary word.
- Ordinary prose that is not a comparison or list.

expl.label: First sub-word fragment of rare multi-token names/words (bipolar)
expl.positive_pole: The first token of a rare word that the tokenizer has split into pieces. These are mostly proper names (people, places, brands, institutions) and some uncommon common words. The activation sits on the word-initial fragment, before the rest of the word appears. Examples: Moiz «Sy»ed (+10), «W»adham College (+8), «Tar»bet, «Ch»orlton, «Ch»autauqua, «Ch»iswell, «Mer»iden, «T»avira, Zhou Xia«oh»u, Katie «Cru»ice, «Pro»enza Schouler, Alison «H»irst, «N»UI Maynooth (all ~+5 to +6). Common-word cases include «gr»inds, «gr»unge, «gr»ating, «gr»annish and white-lipped «pe»ccary (~+6). Weaker cases (+2 to +4): R«ic»ciardo, P«iz» Boè, «Ro»straver, «Du»Pont, «Tw»entekanaal, «Fest»ivals, Madeleine «H»inde, e-«br»ake. A preceding 'at'/'in'/'and' before the name sometimes gets +1. There is also a secondary positive response (+1 to +5) on scattered words in site-description boilerplate, e.g. comment-moderation text ('screening', 'informed', 'engage', 'aims').
expl.negative_pole: The same kind of token: the first fragment of a rare multi-token name or word, but with negative sign. Examples: GVSU's «Me»ijer (-6), «Me»ža prospekts (-5), Mall «Ar»tha Gading (-5), Madeleine «Re»es (-5), «Str»atford upon Avon (-5), «par»rots (-5), «Car»leton College (-5), «lo»ath (-6), thilo «sar»razin (-4), «par»quet (-3), «gre»be (-3), Rain «Sp»outs (-3). It is also negative on repository and website boilerplate. Examples: 'Full text not available «from» this repository' (-7, the strongest negative), and the Wikia ad-blocker notice, where 'Wikia' gets -2 to -3, 'modified' -3 and 'is «not» accessible' -5.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 on almost all tokens; only about 0.2% of tokens reach |value|≥1. Only consider word-initial fragments of rare or foreign words that the tokenizer splits into multiple pieces, mostly proper nouns. Continuation fragments are usually ~0, occasionally ±1 to 3. Ordinary common words, and names that are a single token, stay at 0. Magnitude is typically 3–6, rarely up to 10, and the sign is hard to predict. Lean positive (+5/+6) for fragments like 'Ch', 'gr', 'T', 'W', 'Sy', 'Mer', 'Cru', 'H' starting British/US place names or personal surnames. Lean negative (-5) for fragments like 'Me', 'Ar', 'Re', 'Str', 'Car', 'par', 'lo'. If unsure, predict about ±3 for such fragments. For boilerplate site notices, assign scattered ±1 to 5 values. Use -5 to -7 on 'not' in 'Wikia is not accessible' and on 'from' in 'Full text not available from'. Use +2 to +5 on words in 'we moderate comments / website aims to engage' blurbs. Normal prose, recipes and news text get 0.

expl.label: Lowercase ' un' prefix token, as a standalone subword in mid-sentence words
expl.positive_pole: The standalone subword token ' un' (lowercase, with a leading space) when it begins a word that the tokenizer splits as ' un' + stem. Examples: un|reported, un|cles, un|secured, un|-usable, un|asked, un|controlled, un|hide, un|wise, un|forgeable, un|traceable, un|movable, un|obtainable, un|plug, un|attended, un|professional. It fires whether ' un' is the negating prefix or just the first piece of a word like 'uncles' or 'unquote'. It is strongest in running mid-sentence prose. The activation sits entirely on the ' un' token. The following stem token is ~0. Similar word-initial split prefixes get weaker activation: ' er'(adicating/asing) ~3, ' se'(aring) ~3, ' ca'(utions) ~4, ' ir'(ritable) ~2. Fused prefixes like ' uns'(uitable), ' unt'(itled), ' ut', ' lib', ' so' give ~1.
expl.negative_pole: Weak, max about -3. It comes from capitalized 'Un' at the start of a line, list item, title, or product name ('- Unlined', 'Unisex Watch', 'Unquestionable', 'Unabashedly', 'Unirse'). It also comes from lowercase 'un' directly after an opening quote mark with no space ('"unremittingly', '“unprecedented', '“unbelievably'), and occasionally from the next fragment ('ab' after 'Un' ≈ -2, '“am|azing' ≈ -1).
expl.rubric: Background is 0 on almost all tokens. Lowercase ' un' token with a leading space, in the middle of a sentence: +7 to +10, typically ~8-9. Lowercase ' un' in more technical or list contexts (unlicensed, unmixing, unedited, unprocessed): +3 to +5. Other short split word-start prefixes (' er', ' se', ' ca', ' ir'): +2 to +4. Fused multi-letter prefix tokens (' uns', ' unt', ' ut'): ~+1. Words where 'un' is not split off as its own token (e.g. 'under', 'until', 'unique' as whole tokens): 0. Capitalized 'Un' at a line start, after a bullet, or in a title: -2 to -3. 'un' right after an opening quote with no space: -2 to -3. Stem tokens after 'un': 0.

expl.label: Anticipates an upcoming intention/purpose word (intent, intended, desire, willingness)
expl.positive_pole: Negligible. Only rare, weak (~+1) blips on unrelated tokens, e.g. 'is' in 'This page is best viewed', or name fragments ('G' in Griezmann, 'D' in MK Dons). No coherent pattern.
expl.negative_pole:
Fires on the token immediately BEFORE a likely word of intention, purpose, design or volition. That next word is something like intention(s), intent, intended, desire, willingness, purpose, meant, designated (for), 'for personal use', 'up to you', 'on your mind'. The activation sits on the predicting slot, which is usually a possessive, determiner, copula, negation or modifier. Examples:
- 'announces **his** [intention]' -10
- 'with **the** [explicit intent]' -10
- 'it**'s** [up to you]' -8
- 'is **not** [intended]' -3
- 'increased **their** [willingness]' -7
- 'the one it **was** [designated for]' -6
- 'retain their **original** [public meaning]' -6
- 'all **good** [intentions]' -5
- 'have **no** [desire]' -3
- 'This pattern **is** [for personal use only]' -4
- 'what **was** [on your mind]' -4
- 'had **malicious** [code/intent]' -6
Similar anticipatory slots also fire weakly, such as tokens before a stated consequence or function ('This led to', 'fund is insurance', 'scallops also brought'). Nearby tokens in the same clause often show small negatives (-1 to -2).
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 on almost every token (|v|>=1 on only ~0.1% of tokens).

Assign negatives only where the next word is strongly predicted to be an intention, purpose or volition word:
- Very strong frame, where the possessive or determiner directly precedes 'intention/intent' (e.g. 'announced his', 'with the [explicit] intent'): -8 to -10.
- Copula, negation or possessive before 'intended/willingness/designated/up to': -4 to -8.
- Weaker or more ambiguous purpose/consequence predictions ('This [led to]', 'is [for personal use]', 'Was it your [first time]'): -3 to -7.
- Surrounding clause tokens: -1 to -2.

The intention word itself (intention, intent, desire) usually gets about 0 or only a small value. Do not mark it strongly; the activation is on the slot before it.

Positive values: essentially never; at most +1 on random tokens.

Generic uses of 'the', 'his', 'is' that are not leading into a purpose or intention word are 0.

expl.label: Newline after title/header lines; negative on first subword of rare proper names
expl.positive_pole: Fires at the boundary right after a short title-like or header line. It peaks on the newline token that ends a headline, product name, section title, or advisory heading, at the point where body text is about to start (e.g. 'Hydra v 7.4: Fast Network cracker↵', 'Cloud Controller API regression↵'). It also fires on header-marker words inside email or forum separators, such as 'Forwarded Mail =' in '=====Forwarded Mail=====' and 'next part' in '---- next part ----'. Weaker activations come from 'Table of Contents↵', 'Editor's Notes', and separator underscores before 'EXAMPLE'.
expl.negative_pole: Fires on the first subword token of an uncommon proper name that is split into several pieces, mostly surnames and place names. Gaelic 'Mc'/'Mac' prefixes are typical, as in 'Mc|Leod', 'Mc|Eachran', 'Mac|leod Trail' and 'Mac Thornberry'. Indian and other foreign place names also trigger it ('Ch|alisgaon', 'P|ottstown', 'M|uleshoe', 'Kom|bo', 'P|lovdiv'), as do names like 'Ak|ers' and 'Ak|ashi'. The activation sits on the initial fragment, and later fragments are near 0. It is stronger when the name appears in a list or after a title or role such as 'by', 'Reps.', or 'Hon.'.
expl.rubric:
Background is 0 for almost all tokens, since activity is very sparse.

Positive values:
- +5 to +10: a newline right after a standalone title or headline line, or the 'Mail'/'=' tokens in a forwarded-mail banner.
- +2 to +4: newlines after section headings ('Table of Organization↵', 'Table of Contents↵'), after a dateline in an advisory, or after a short product or event name; also 'part' in 'next part'.
- +1 to +2: weaker heading-like line ends, separator lines, and the preceding header words ('Forward', 'ouncements').
- Ordinary sentence-ending newlines in running prose are about 0, or at most +1 to +2 when the line looks like a heading.

Negative values:
- -5 to -7: the first piece of a rare multi-token proper name (Mc/Mac/Ak/P/M/Ch + rest).
- -1 to -3: the first piece of a moderately rare name or term ('M|irepoix', 'P.L.', 'Am|alija', 'Str|aczinksy').
- Common names that are a single token, and the later subword pieces of a name, are about 0.

expl.label: + first subword of rare surnames; − slot predicting 'spirit(s)'
expl.positive_pole: First subword token of an unfamiliar, usually foreign proper name (most often a surname) that the tokenizer splits into pieces. It typically follows a known first name: Jean Michel «G»athy, David «P»ocock, Marcello «L»ippi, Jacques «Leg»rand, Bill «Le»avy, Fela «K»uti, Taapsee «P»annu, Paddy «P»imblett, Eugene «C»ernan, Marie «L»aveau. Only the first fragment fires; later pieces stay near 0. The same applies more weakly to other split rare words: place names (Mer|iden), Latin or foreign titles (Gaudium, Vivit, Corpus Reformatorum), German compound pieces (Infanterieregiment, beruf), Japanese katakana fragments, 'g'entry, 'Be'ers.
expl.negative_pole: Tokens where the next word is likely 'spirit/spirits' (or a near synonym such as soul, essence, ghost), usually the determiner or adjective just before it. Examples: 'encapsulate «the» spirit' (-10), 'awaken «that» spirit' (-9), 'symbolizes the «collective» strength, spirit' (-9), 'sends «the» spirits off' (-9), 'festive spirit' (-7), 'artisanal spirit' (-6), 'wine, beer «and» spirits' (-5), 'soul, flesh «and» skeleton' (-8), 'witches «or» devils' (-7). It also fires in Chinese and Korean contexts about ghosts or souls. Weaker negatives (-3 to -1) appear on related abstract virtue/collaboration phrasing: 'the collaborative approach', 'foster', 'grow in their faith'.
expl.rubric: Background is 0 on almost all tokens; |value|≥1 occurs on only about 0.1% of tokens. Positive: first subword of a split rare surname right after a given name scores +4 to +6. A rare place or foreign title fragment scores +2 to +4. Common or well-known names that are single tokens score 0, as do continuation subwords. Negative: a determiner, adjective, or conjunction right before an expected 'spirit(s)' / 'essence' / 'soul' scores -5 to -10. The word 'spirit' itself is near 0. Loosely related contexts (faith, collaboration, alcohol lists) score -1 to -4. Ordinary prose, numbers, and technical text score 0.
